BURHAN:v1p91/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p91/r3.speaker: صاحب الفنون
BURHAN:v1p91/r3.claim: If creation's glorification means signs and blessings that should prompt reflection, human failure to notice them merits reproach; God's forbearance and forgiveness excuse this neglect.
BURHAN:v1p91/r3.anchor: أجاب صاحب الفنون بثلاثة أوجه أحدها إن فسرنا التسبيح على ما درج فى الأشياء من العبر

BURHAN:v1p91/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p91/r4.speaker: صاحب الفنون
BURHAN:v1p91/r4.claim: If animals literally glorify in their own languages, they praise without sin while humans disobey; the closing appeal to forbearance and forgiveness therefore concerns human disobedience.
BURHAN:v1p91/r4.anchor: أجاب صاحب الفنون بثلاثة أوجه أحدها إن فسرنا التسبيح على ما درج فى الأشياء من العبر

BURHAN:v1p91/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p91/r5.speaker: صاحب الفنون
BURHAN:v1p91/r5.claim: A third explanation links the ending to the opening assertion that heavens and earth glorify God, and to 42:5, where angels glorify and seek forgiveness for earth's people; the verse can thus cover neglected reflection and forgiven disobedience.
BURHAN:v1p91/r5.anchor: أجاب صاحب الفنون بثلاثة أوجه أحدها إن فسرنا التسبيح على ما درج فى الأشياء من العبر

BURHAN:v1p91/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p91/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p91/r6.claim: An unattributed hadith says that without grazing beasts, bowed elders, and suckling children, punishment would be poured down upon people.
BURHAN:v1p91/r6.anchor: وفى الحديث لولا بهائم رتع وشيوخ ركع وأطفال رضع لصب عليكم العذاب صبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r11.claim: One view takes the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants as literally uttering glorification, with God granting speech even to things without life or growth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r11.anchor: حمله بعضهم على النطق بالتسبيح حقيقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r12.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r12.claim: ʿIkrima says living creatures glorify literally: a tree does so, but a column does not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r12.anchor: وبه قال عكرمة قال: الشجرة تسبح والأسطوانة لا تسبح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r13.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a wooden dining tray once glorified when it was a tree, but ceased when it became dead wood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r13.anchor: وسئل الحسن عن الخوان أيسبح؟ فقال: قد كان تسبح مرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r14.claim: Another view reads the glorification of inanimate things metaphorically: their condition points to the Maker, power, wisdom, and perfection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54/r14.anchor: وقيل: التسبيح المنسوب لما لا يعقل مجاز ومعناه أنها تسبح بلسان الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r1.claim: The address that people do not understand the glorification targets polytheists: their acknowledgment of God as Creator is contradicted by their associating other gods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r1.anchor: ويكون قوله: ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم خطابا للمشركين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r2.claim: A metaphorical account can apply commonly to all creation, while angels, humans, and jinn also glorify literally; he avoids assigning metaphor and literal meaning to the same word at once.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r2.anchor: فيكون التسبيح المسند إلى السموات والأرض ومن فيهن على سبيل المجاز قدرا مشتركا بين الجميع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the relative pronoun man treats heavens and earth as rational because glorification is predicated of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية ثم أعاد على السموات والأرض ضمير من يعقل لما أسند إليها فعل العاقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r4.claim: He rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s assumption that hun is limited to rational feminine plurals; it can refer broadly to feminine plurals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r4.anchor: وليس كما تخيل بل هن يكون ضمير الجمع المؤنث مطلقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r5.claim: The two grammarians, Ḥamza, and Ḥafṣ read tasbaḥ with tāʾ; the remaining seven read yasbaḥ with yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ النحويان وحزة وحفص: تسبح بالتاء من فوق وباقي السبعة بالياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r6.claim: The codex reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh, al-Aʿmash, and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif has the feminine past-tense form sabbaḥat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r6.anchor: وفي بعض المصاحف سبحت له السموات بلفظ الماضي وتاء التأنيث وهي قراءة عبد الله والأعمش وطلحة بن مصرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r7.claim: God is forbearing by delaying punishment for their bad judgment, and forgiving if they return and affirm divine unity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p54#2/r7.anchor: إنه كان حليما حيث لا يعاجلكم بالعقوبة على سوء نظركم غفورا إن رجعتم ووحدتم الله تعالى

TABATABAI:12:22-34#25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#25/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#25/r4.claim: Created things praise God through their beauty and point to His majesty through their need and imperfection; lovers see them as signs rather than independent realities.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#25/r4.anchor: فالأشياء من جهة أنواع خلقها وحسنها تدل على جماله الذي لا يتناهى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Tasbīḥ absolves God of negative traits; when joined with praise, it affirms His higher attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The real meaning of ﺗﺴﺒﻴﺢis to absolve someone of negative traits.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God grants humans limited freedom, which they misuse by making whatever accusations against Him they wish.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God has blessed people with the freedom to exercise their will in a certain sphere.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: All creatures between the heavens and earth glorify God, even though people do not understand their glorification.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the seven heavens and the earth and all the creatures found between them all glorify God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Their ascription of partners is so grave that the heavens would have fallen upon them; God's benevolence and forgiveness nevertheless grant them respite despite their misdeeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Such is the grave nature of their ascribing partners to God that the heavens would have fallen on them.

BURSEVI:v5p124/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p124/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p124/r1.claim: Tasbīḥ is declaring God free of the defects of possibility and origination; the heavens and earth do so by the signs of their existence, power, and wisdom, while their inhabitants speak praise aloud.
BURSEVI:v5p124/r1.anchor: التسبيح تنزيه الحق وتبعيده عن نقائص الإمكان والحدوث

BURSEVI:v5p124/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p124/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p124/r2.claim: The verse's generality encompasses both spoken praise and the mute signs of createdness that testify to God's transcendence.
BURSEVI:v5p124/r2.anchor: معنى منتظم لما ينطق به لسان المقال ولسان الحال بطريق عموم المجاز

BURSEVI:v5p124/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p124/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p124/r3.claim: Every thing, whether animal or plant, indicates its Maker, power, and wisdom; polytheists fail to understand because their defective reflection does not follow their admission that God created the heavens and earth.
BURSEVI:v5p124/r3.anchor: من الأشياء حيوانا كان أو نباتا يدل على الصانع وقدرته وحكمته

BURSEVI:v5p124/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p124/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p124/r4.claim: God's forbearance delays requital despite their heedlessness and associationism, and He forgives those who repent and return to unity.
BURSEVI:v5p124/r4.anchor: ولذلك لم يعاجلكم بالعقوبة مع أنتم عليه من الإعراض عن التدبر

BURSEVI:v5p124/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p124/r5.speaker: الزمخشري والبيضاوي وأبو السعود
BURSEVI:v5p124/r5.claim: The exoteric commentators explain the failure to understand praise by the polytheists' neglect of sound reflection and their failure to follow their admission of the Creator.
BURSEVI:v5p124/r5.anchor: هذا ما عليه الزمخشري والبيضاوي وأبو السعود ومن يليهم من أهل الظاهر

BURSEVI:v5p124/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p124/r6.speaker: علي السمرقندي
BURSEVI:v5p124/r6.claim: He reports that the righteous early Muslims take both occurrences of tasbīḥ literally, and calls this the sounder view: if inanimate speech is possible, its praise should be accepted too.
BURSEVI:v5p124/r6.anchor: ذهب السلف الصالح إلى أن التسبيح في الآية في المحلين محمول على حقيقته وهو الأصح

BURSEVI:v5p126/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p126/r1.speaker: أهل الحقيقة
BURSEVI:v5p126/r1.claim: They apply “you do not understand” to Muslims and polytheists alike: hearing sounds is insufficient without reflecting on what the speaker conveys and praising God accordingly.
BURSEVI:v5p126/r1.anchor: عام للمسلمين والمشركين أي : لا تسمعون فلا تفقهون تسبيحهم

BURSEVI:v5p126/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p126/r2.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v5p126/r2.claim: He says created things praise in languages unlike human languages, though God may let some servants, such as David and Solomon, understand some inanimate beings and animals.
BURSEVI:v5p126/r2.anchor: لأنه ليس بلغتكم ويجوز أن يفهم تعالى بعض عباده تسبيح بعض الجمادات والعجماوات كداود وسليمان

BURSEVI:v5p126/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p126/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p126/r3.claim: He rejects language difference as a sufficient explanation: some beings have varied, audible sounds while others have no audible sound, yet all are affirmed to praise.
BURSEVI:v5p126/r3.anchor: لأن لغات ماله أصوات مختلفة لا تفقه وإن كانت مسموعة

BURSEVI:v5p126/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p126/r4.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
BURSEVI:v5p126/r4.claim: Salmi transmits from him that all created beings praise God in different languages, but only a divinely learned heart with opened inner hearing can hear and understand them.
BURSEVI:v5p126/r4.anchor: سلمى از ابو عثمان مغربي قدس سرهما نقل ميكندكه تمام مكونات باختلاف لغات تسبيح الهي ميكويند

BURSEVI:v5p126/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p126/r5.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v5p126/r5.claim: He offers two explanations for a stone's speech: God may create life and intelligence with it, or create a sound without life.
BURSEVI:v5p126/r5.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون نطق الحجر كلاما مقرونا بحياة وعلم ويحتمل أن يكون صوتا مجردا

BURSEVI:v5p126/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p126/r6.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
BURSEVI:v5p126/r6.claim: Against those who deny cognition to inanimate things, he says life permeates the world; all things hearing the call to prayer can testify, though God veils this life from humans and jinn except chosen knowers, who directly hear their praise and speech.
BURSEVI:v5p126/r6.anchor: سر الحياة سار في جميع العالم وقد ورد أن كل شيء سمع صوت المؤذن من رطب ويابس يشهد له

BURSEVI:v5p126/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p126/r7.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
BURSEVI:v5p126/r7.claim: A mountain crumbled at the manifestation because it knew God's greatness; without that apprehension it would not have crumbled.
BURSEVI:v5p126/r7.anchor: وكذلك اندكاك الجبل لما وقع التجلي إنما كان ذلك منه لمعرفته بعظمة الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r1.claim: Every particle glorifies God: living beings praise in their own tongues, while inanimate things use a heavenly tongue; their praise thanks Him for bringing them into being and nurturing them, unlike human praise.
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r1.anchor: ينزهه عما يقولون من كل نقيصة ذرات المكونات وأجزاء المخلوقات

BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r2.claim: Each particle has a spiritual kingdom: the afterlife is living rather than inert, so every particle has a spiritual tongue that praises its Maker and thanks Him for His gifts.
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r2.anchor: الملكوت باطن الكون وهو الآخرة والآخرة حيوان لا جماد

BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r3.claim: This spiritual speech explains the pebbles praising in the Prophet's hand, the earth recounting its news, body parts testifying, and heaven and earth answering God's command.
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r3.anchor: وبهذا اللسان نطق الحصى في يد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبهذا تنطق الأرض يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r4.claim: God was forbearing from eternity in bringing into being those who would associate partners with Him, and forgives those who repent of such claims.
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r4.anchor: في الأزل إذ أخرج من العدم من يتولد منه أن يتخذ مع الله آلهة أخرى

BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r5.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r5.claim: Each thing's distinctive property, longing for and preserving what completes it, manifests its uniqueness and implicitly declares God one; its pursuit of perfection denies deficiency, and its display of perfection praises its giver.
BURSEVI:v5p127#2/r5.anchor: لكل شيء خاصية لا يشاركه فيها غيره وكما لا يخصه دون ما عداه يشتاقه ويطلبه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو والأخوان وحفص
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r1.claim: They read tasbiḥ with the feminine verb form; the other readers use the masculine form because the subject's grammatical femininity is nonliteral and separated from the verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r1.anchor: بالفوقانية وهي قراءة أبي عمرو والأخوين وحفص

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r2.speaker: الباقون
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r2.claim: They read the verb in the masculine form because the feminine subject is nonliteral and separated from the verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتحتانية لأن تأنيث الفاعل مجازي مع الفصل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r3.claim: A past-tense reading, sabbaḥat, is also transmitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r3.anchor: وقريء ( سبحت ) ( له السموات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r4.claim: The seven heavens, earth, and all within them include angels and humans and jinn; every kind of thing, animate, plant, or mineral, glorifies God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r4.anchor: أي من الملائكة والثقلين ( وإن من شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r5.claim: The primary interpretation takes glorification as the testimony of created possibility and origination: each thing demonstrates God's necessary existence, unity, power, and freedom from contingent properties.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r5.anchor: والمراد من التسبيح الدلالة بلسان الحال أي تدل بإمكانها وحدوثها دلالة واضحة على وجوب وجوده تعالى ووحدته

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r6.claim: This is a transferred metaphor, as when one says that a state speaks; a representational metaphor is also possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r6.anchor: ففي الكلام استعارة تبعية كما في نطقت الحال وجوز أن يعتبر فيه استعارة تمثيلية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r7.claim: The failure to understand applies to the polytheists and disbelievers just described, not humanity universally; the passage follows their false attributions with all creation's testimony against them.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r7.anchor: لما أن الخطاب للمشركين والكفرة لا للناس على العموم لأنه تقدم ذكر قبائحهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r8.claim: The closing description means God is forbearing, delaying punishment for their failure to reason correctly, and forgives those who repent and reflect.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r8.anchor: أي إنه سبحانه حليم ولذلك لم يعاجلكم بالعقوبة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r9.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r9.claim: Ibn al-Munīr argues that the closing promise cannot address polytheists because God does not forgive their association; he takes the addressees as believers who fail to comprehend inanimate speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r9.anchor: وظن ابن المنير أن هذا التذييل يأبى كون الخطاب للمشركين قال : لأنه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r10.claim: Alusi rejects Ibn al-Munīr's reading because it breaks the passage's coherence; the closing phrase does not prevent the direct address to disbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83/r10.anchor: وليس بسديد لخروج الكلام على ذلك من النظام ووجه التذييل ما سمعت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r1.claim: Another reading combines actual verbal glorification with state-based testimony, either as a general figurative usage or by combining literal and figurative senses; different creatures may use different modes.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r1.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالتسبيح الدلالة على تنزيه الباري سبحانه عن لوازم الامكان وتوابع الحدوث مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r2.claim: A difficulty for the combined reading is that some verbal glorification is understood by polytheists; replies say they fail to reflect or benefit, or that failure to grasp one aspect counts as not understanding all.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r2.anchor: لأن من ذلك التسبيح ما يفقهه المشركون وغيرهم وهو التسبيح القالي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r3.speaker: بعض الظاهرية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r3.claim: Some literalists hold that every creature, including inanimate things, glorifies God with actual speech.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib endorses the literal interpretation that all things verbally glorify God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r4.anchor: وارتضاه الراغب وقال في تفسير الخازن إنه الأصح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r5.speaker: الخازن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r5.claim: Al-Khāzin calls the universal, literal verbal interpretation the soundest view.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r5.anchor: وقال في تفسير الخازن إنه الأصح على أن التسبيح على معناه الحقيقي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r6.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r6.claim: The Imam objects that literal verbal glorification requires knowledge, which inanimate things lack because they lack life; otherwise the condition for knowledge would collapse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r6.anchor: لأن هذا التسبيح لا يحصل إلا مع العلم وهو مما يتصور في الجماد لفقد شرطه العقلي وهو الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r7.claim: He also argues that the closing rebuke makes ignorance of verbal praise culpable, whereas failing to understand inanimate speech would not be a sin; ignorance of their testimony through signs is culpable.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r7.anchor: وأيضا التذييل السابق يأبى ذلك لدلالته على أن عدم فقه التسبيح المذكور جرم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r8.claim: Reports and traditions strongly attest to audible praise; one sound report describes pebbles glorifying in the Prophet's hand.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r8.anchor: ومن تتبع الأحاديث والآثار رأي فيها ما يشهد بما ذهب إليه هذا البعض شهادة لا تكاد تقبل التأويل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r9.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r9.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said a dish of thريد was glorifying; several companions heard it, and the Prophet had the dish passed among them.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p83#2/r9.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ عن أنس قال : أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بطعام ثريد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the Companions counted signs as blessings; while water flowed between the Prophet's fingers, they heard its sound and glorification as they drank.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : كنا أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم نعد الآيات بركة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet's account that Noah, at death, urged his sons to say Subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdihi, the prayer of everything and means by which everything receives provision.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : إنا نوحا عليه السلام لما حضرته الوفاة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r3.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r3.claim: Muʿādh ibn Anas reports the Prophet forbidding people to burden mounts as seats for roadside and market conversations; a mount may remember God more than its rider.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r3.anchor: وأخرج أحمد عن معاذ بن أنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه مر على قوم وهم وقوفا على دواب لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet's prohibition on killing frogs, saying their croaking is glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال : نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قتل الضفدع وقال نقيقها تسبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r5.claim: Anas reports that an angel taught David to hear a frog praising God in words David had not used; David vowed to praise God with that praise.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r5.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال : ظن داود عليه السلام في نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r6.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r6.claim: In a long report from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, David hears that seventy thousand frogs stand on one leg glorifying God, correcting his thought that no one else praised God at that hour.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r6.anchor: وأخرج أحمد في الزهد وأبو الشيخ عن شهر بن حوسب من حديث طويل أن داود علي السلام أتى البحر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r7.claim: ʿAlī reports from the Prophet that birds glorify their Lord each morning and ask Him for that day's provision.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r7.anchor: عن أبي ضمرة قال : كنا عند علي بن الحسين رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r8.claim: A report through al-Zuhrī from Abū Bakr says that game hunted, trees cut, and branches severed are due to the scarcity of glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p84/r8.anchor: وأخرجوأخرج ابن راهوية في مسنده من طريق الزهري

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء وابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r1.claim: A marfūʿ report from Abū al-Dardāʾ and Ibn Masʿūd gives the same account that hunting and cutting vegetation result from deficient glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن الشيخ عن أبي الدرداء وابن مردوية عن ابن مسعود مثل ذلك مرفوعا أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that without the veil hiding the glorification of what is in people's homes, they could not live together.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r2.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ عن الحسن لولا ما غم عليكم من تسبيح ما معكم من البيوت ما تقاررتم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r3.speaker: لوط بن أبي لوط
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r3.claim: A report ascribed to Luṭ ibn Abī Luṭ assigns a distinct formula of glorification to each of the seven heavens.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r3.anchor: عن أبي حاتم عن لوط بن أبي لوط قال : بلغني أن تسبيح سماء الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r4.claim: Taken together, these reports support actual verbal glorification; this is also the Sufi position, whose spiritual wayfarers may hear things praising God in diverse tongues.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r4.anchor: وهي بمجموعها متعاضدة في الدلالة على أن التسبيح قالي كما لا يخفى وهو مذهب الصوفية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r5.claim: Some early Muslims reportedly heard certain inanimate objects glorifying God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r5.anchor: وقد روي عن بعض السلف سماعا لتسبيح بعض الجمادات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r6.claim: One view says all things glorify without restriction; another gives conditions under which dust, beads, leaves, garments, beasts, and birds cease glorifying.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r6.anchor: واختلف القائلون بهذا التسبيح فقال بعضهم : بثبوته للأشياء مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r7.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r7.claim: When someone said a table was glorifying, al-Ḥasan replied that only things remaining in their original state do so.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r7.anchor: عن ابن شوذب قال : جلس الحسن مع أصحابه على مائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r8.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says every thing still in its original state and not dead glorifies God; death may mean departure from that original state.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r8.anchor: عن السدي أنه قال : ما من شيء على أصله الأول لم يمت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r9.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r9.claim: Qatāda limits glorification to things with a spirit, such as trees and animals; treating trees as living follows ordinary language about a dried tree dying.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r9.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قال في الآية : كل شيء فيه الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r10.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās excludes donkeys and dogs from the universal glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال كل شيء يسبح إلا الحمار والكلب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r1.claim: Alusi sees no basis for excluding those animals, doubts the report's attribution to Ibn ʿAbbās, and finds no reason to prefer its restriction over the many unqualified reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r1.anchor: ولا أرى لاستثناء ما ذكر وجها وفي القلب من صحة الرواية عن الحبر شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r2.claim: To answer the objection that verbal praise requires awareness, some posit a fitting kind of life and knowledge in every thing, whose reality only God knows.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r2.anchor: وتقصى بعضهم عن هذا بالتزام أن لكل شيء حياة وعلما لائقين به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r3.speaker: الخواص
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r3.claim: Al-Khawwāṣ, as quoted by al-Shaʿrānī, says every inanimate thing understands speech and feels pain as an animal does.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r3.anchor: عن الخواص أنه قال : كل جماد يفهم الخطاب ويتألم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r4.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r4.claim: The Greatest Shaykh says minerals and plants possess spirits normally hidden from perception; all things are living, speaking, and glorifying, though their forms differ by temperament.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r4.anchor: وقال الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره : أن المسمى بالجماد والنبات له عندنا أرواح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r5.claim: The report that an announcer's voice is witnessed by every wet and dry thing, together with prophetic law and revelation, supports this account of creaturely awareness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r5.anchor: وقد رود أن المؤذن يشهد له مدى صوته من رطب ويابس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r6.claim: A report about the Prophet's prayer for fever addresses it as a conscious being and directs it to leave for someone who alleges other gods.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r6.anchor: واستدل بعضهم في هذا المقام بما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في دعائه للحمى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r7.speaker: السجاد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r7.claim: The al-Ṣaḥīfa contains an address to the moon that appears to ascribe awareness to it; reports also describe ʿUmar writing to the Nile and speaking to the earth during an earthquake.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r7.anchor: وجاء عن السجاد رضي الله تعالى عنه في الصحيفة في مخاطبة القمر ما هو ظاهر في أنه له شعورا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r8.claim: There is no need to allegorize such reports: no one claims inanimate awareness resembles ordinary animal perception, and believers should trust truthful reports while recognizing their own limited knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p85#2/r8.anchor: لا أحد يقول : إن شعور الجمادات كشعور الحيوانات الظاهرة بحيث

ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r1.claim: On the universal-life interpretation, the pronoun in tasbīḥahum needs no special explanation; another proposal attaches the closing statement to God's transcendence, but that move is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r1.anchor: وعلى هذا الذي ذكروه لا تحتاج إعادة ضمير ذوي العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r2.claim: Alusi's preferred reconciliation allows both state-based and verbal glorification in every thing, with the rebuke about failure to understand directed to deficient grasp of state-based testimony.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r2.anchor: ولعل الأولى فيه أن يلتزم حمل التسبيح على ما هو الأعم من الحالي والقالي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r3.claim: Since some beings attributed glorification are deniers or silent, a figurative reading is required; the response is that context implicitly excludes them, despite an extravagant claim that even deniers sanctify God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r3.anchor: ويشكل أيضا أن من أفراد من نسب إليه التسبيح الجحد فضلا عن الساكت فالحمل على المجاز واجب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r4.claim: A passive intensive reading, lā yufqahū, is also transmitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p86/r4.anchor: وقريء ( لا يفقهون ) على صيغة المبني للمفعول من باب التفعيل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r5.claim: Sufi authorities say created things praise God verbally, though only those granted nearness or illumination hear it; the Prophet's companions heard pebbles praise in his gathering.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r5.anchor: من أنه قالي إلا أنه لا يسمعه إلا من فاز بقرب النوافل أو من أشرق عليه شيء من أنواره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r6.claim: All Muslims accept praise by a thing's state; Sufis explain it through each thing's distinctive property, its longing for what it lacks, and its display of perfection, each declaring God uniquely perfect.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r6.anchor: والتسبيح الحالي مما لا ينكره أحد من المسلمين وقرره بعض الصوفية بأن لكل شيء خاصية ليست لغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r7.claim: By this analogy the heavens praise through perfection, influence, and lordship, the earth through creation and provision, and angels through knowledge, power, and immateriality.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p125/r7.anchor: والملائكة بالعلم والقدرة والتجرد عن المادة على القول بأنهم أرواح مجردة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p95/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p95/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وحفص ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p95/r10.claim: These reciters read “the heavens glorify” with the feminine verb; the rest use the masculine because a separation intervenes before the feminine subject.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p95/r10.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وحفص ويعقوب: " تسبح " بالتاء وقرأ الآخرون بالياء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says every living thing glorifies God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: وإن من شيء حي إلا يسبح بحمده.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r2.claim: The things glorifying God are animals and growing plants.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r3.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r3.claim: Trees glorify God, but a column does not.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة: الشجرة تسبح والأسطوانة لا تسبح.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r4.speaker: المقدام بن معد يكرب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r4.claim: Al-Miqdām reports that many created things glorify only in certain states: damp earth, a lifted bead, a fallen leaf, a soiled garment, still water, and silent animals and birds cease.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r4.anchor: عن المقدام بن معد يكرب قال: إن التراب يسبح ما لم يبتل فإذا ابتل ترك التسبيح وإن الخرزة تسبح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r5.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r5.claim: Every inanimate thing glorifies God, even a door creaking or a ceiling cracking.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r5.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: وإن من شيء جماد إلا يسبح بحمده حتى صرير الباب ونقيض السقف.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r6.claim: Every thing, living, dead, or inanimate, glorifies God with the words “Glory and praise be to God.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كل الأشياء تسبح لله حيا كان أو ميتا أو جمادا، وتسبيحها سبحان الله وبحمده.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r7.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that the Companions saw the Prophet's fingers produce water and heard food glorifying while being eaten.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: كنا نعد الآيات بركة وأنتم تعدونها تخويفا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r8.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r8.claim: A figurative interpretation takes creation as glorifying through subtle construction and wondrous form that point to its Creator.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r8.anchor: وسائر الحيوانات سوى العقلاء ما دلت بلطيف تركيبها وعجيب هيئتها على خالقها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r9.claim: The literal reports transmitted from the early generations are preferred over the figurative account.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r10.claim: God knows a reality of inanimate things that no one else can know, so its knowledge should be entrusted to Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96/r10.anchor: واعلم أن لله تعالى علما في الجمادات لا يقف عليه غيره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96#2/r1.claim: People do not understand the glorification of things that do not praise God in human languages and tongues.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p96#2/r1.anchor: أي لا تعلمون تسبيح ما عدا من يسبح بلغاتكم وألسنتكم

QASHANI:17:44/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:44/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:44/r1.claim: Every thing has a unique property and perfection it seeks when absent and preserves when attained; manifesting it declares God's uniqueness, requests completion from the Perfect, and displays that completion.
QASHANI:17:44/r1.anchor: إن لكل شيء خاصية ليست لغيره، وكمالا يخصه دون ما عداه

QASHANI:17:44/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:44/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:44/r2.claim: Creatures glorify through their qualities: skies by permanence, elevation, influence, creation, and lordship; earth by stability, origination, sustenance, nurture, mercy, and rewarding obedience; angels through knowledge and power, and immaterial beings through transcendence.
QASHANI:17:44/r2.anchor: والأرض بالدوام والثبات والخلاقية والرزاقية والتربية والإشفاق والرحمة

QASHANI:17:44/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:44/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:44/r3.claim: People fail to understand this glorification because they scarcely contemplate the unseen or listen attentively; only a living, present heart perceives it.
QASHANI:17:44/r3.anchor: لقلة النظر والفكر في ملكوت الأشياء وعدم الإصغاء إليهم

QASHANI:17:44/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:44/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:44/r4.claim: God's forbearance delays punishment while people neglect their glorification; understanding creatures' unity and praise is among human beings' own distinctive perfections, and God forgives their neglect.
QASHANI:17:44/r4.anchor: من خواصكم تفقه تسبيحهم وتوحيده كما وحدوه

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r1.claim: The heavens, earth, and all things glorify God by their contingent, created state, which points to the eternal Creator.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r1.anchor: ينزهه عما هو من لوازم الإمكان وتوابع الحدوث بلسان الحال حيث تدل بإمكانها وحدوثها على الصانع القديم الواجب لذاته

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r2.claim: The polytheists fail to understand this glorification because they neglect sound reflection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r2.anchor: لإخلالكم بالنظر الصحيح الذي به يفهم تسبيحهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r3.claim: Alternatively, glorification can encompass both spoken praise and indication, attributed jointly to what can and cannot speak, if a word may carry both meanings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يحمل التسبيح على المشترك بين اللفظ والدلالة لإسناده إلى ما يتصور منه اللفظ وإلى ما لا يتصور منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Nāfiʿ, and Abū Bakr read the verb with yāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر ونافع وأبو بكر «يسبح» بالياء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r5.claim: God is forbearing by not hastening punishment for heedlessness and associating partners, and forgives those who repent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:44/r5.anchor: حيث لم يعاجلكم بالعقوبة على غفلتكم وشرككم.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r2.claim: The heavens, earth, and every being praise God; capable beings do so verbally, and all creation also does so through signs revealed by its existence, order, and finitude.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r2.anchor: وهذا تسبيح بلسان المقال ممن يصح منه , وبلسان الحال منه ومن غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r3.claim: Creation's origination indicates an eternal, uncreated maker; its precision indicates a wise governor, and its passing away indicates a powerful, freely acting sovereign.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r3.anchor: من جهة حدوثها إلى صانع أحدثها قديم غير مصنوع , ومن جهة إتقانها إلى كونه مدبرا حكيما

BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r4.claim: The verse says people do not comprehend creation's praise, rather than that they cannot hear it, because they turn from reflection; ordinary people differ from elect who hear inanimate praise.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r4.anchor: دون ( تسمعون ) { تسبيحهم } لإعراضكم عن النظر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r5.speaker: البخاري عن عبد الله بن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r5.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Ibn Mas'ud's report that on a journey the Prophet put his hand in a small vessel and water flowed between his fingers; companions also heard food glorifying God as it was eaten.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p384/r5.anchor: روى البخاري عن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال : كنا نعد الآيات بركة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r1.claim: The glorification of pebbles is well known; David's Psalms repeatedly exhort readers to reflect on the praise offered by creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r1.anchor: وتسبيح الحصى مشهور , وفي زبور داود عليه السلام تكرير كثير لهذه الآية وحث على تأملها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r2.claim: Psalm 68 says the heavens, earth, seas, and all creatures moving in them praise God.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r2.anchor: تسبح له السماوات والأرض والبحار وكل ما يدب فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r3.claim: Psalm 85 declares that no one compares with God or His works and all created nations come to bow and praise His name because He is great and performs wonders.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r3.anchor: فليس مثلك يا ربي وإلهي ولا مثل أعمالك , لأن جميع الأمم الذين خلقت يأتون ويسجدون أمامك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r4.claim: Psalm 88 praises God's strength over enemies, His ownership of heaven and earth, creation of land and sea, and the praise of Tabor and Hermon; justice and mercy establish His rule.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r4.anchor: لك السماوات ولك الأرض , أنت أسست الدنيا بكمالها , خلقت البر والبحر , تابور وحرمون باسمك يسبحان

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r5.claim: Psalm 95 calls the whole earth to sing a new song, worship in God's holy courts, and tremble before the God who rules the peoples justly.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r5.anchor: سبحوا الرب تسبيحا جديدا , الأرض كلها تسبح الرب , اسجدوا للرب في هياكل قدسه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r6.claim: Psalm 97 says that the whole earth praises God and glorifies Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r6.anchor: ولله تسبح كل الأرض , مجدوا وهللوا وسبحوا الرب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r7.claim: Psalm 148 lists angels, sun, moon, stars, waters, animals, plants, and people as praising the Lord, who created them and set their enduring limits.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r7.anchor: سبحوا الرب من السماوات , سبحوه من العلى يا جميع ملائكته

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r8.claim: Psalm 150 commands praise in God's sanctuary and power, by trumpet and loud sounds, concluding that every breath praises the Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r8.anchor: سبحوا الله في كل قديسيه , سبحوه في جلد قوته , سبحوه كمثل جبروته

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r9.claim: Because creation's praise is clear, people deserve punishment for failing to understand it through neglect of reflection; their safety is only God's forbearance and delayed judgment.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r9.anchor: فكانوا مستحقين للعقاب في عدم فهمه بعدم التأمل في المصنوعات حق التأمل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r10.claim: God is forbearing and does not hasten punishment for turning away from reflection; He is abundantly forgiving, encouraging repentance.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p385/r10.anchor: حيث لا يعاجلكم بالعقوبة على إعراضكم عن صرف الأفكار فيما أمركم بصرفها إليه

DURR-FULL:v5p288/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r3.claim: On the Night Journey to Jerusalem, the Prophet heard the highest heavens glorifying God in a hymn praising the majestic, exalted Lord.
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r3.anchor:
عن عبد الرحمن بن قرط رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة
أسري به إلى المسجد الأقصى

DURR-FULL:v5p288/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r4.speaker: لوط بن أبي لوط
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r4.claim: A report assigns a distinct glorification formula to each heaven, from praise of the Most High in the lowest to God's majesty and dignity in the seventh.
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r4.anchor: عن لوط بن أبي لوط قال: بلغني أن تسبيح سماء الدنيا سبحان ربنا الأعلى والثانية سبحانه وتعالى

DURR-FULL:v5p288/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r5.claim: The sky creaks under its great weight; every span contains an angel prostrating and glorifying God.
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r5.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: وهو جالس مع أصحابه إذ سمع هزة

DURR-FULL:v5p288/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r6.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r6.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet recited تسبح with the feminine tāʾ in this verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p288/r6.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ {تسبح له السماوات السبع والأرض} بالتاء

DURR-FULL:v5p289/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r1.claim: Noah told his son to say سبحان الله, the prayer and glorification of creation and a means by which creatures receive provision.
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا أخبركم بشيء أمر به نوح ابنه

DURR-FULL:v5p289/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r2.speaker: نوح
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r2.claim: At death Noah instructed his two sons to say سبحان الله وبحمده, the prayer of everything and a means by which everything receives provision.
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي اله عنهما: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن نوحا لما حضرته الوفاة قال لابنيه

DURR-FULL:v5p289/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r3.claim: The rooster's cry is its prayer and its wing beating its prostration and bow; the Prophet then recited the verse on universal glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r3.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: صوت الديك صلاته وضربه بجناحيه

DURR-FULL:v5p289/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r4.claim: A caller from heaven tells people to remember God so He remembers them; the rooster hears first and crows, which is its glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: ينادي مناد من السماء اذكروا الله يذكركم فلا يسمعها أول من الديك

DURR-FULL:v5p289/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r5.claim: Do not strike animals in the face, because every creature glorifies God.
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا تضربوا وجوه الدواب

DURR-FULL:v5p289/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r6.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r6.claim: Umar also says not to slap animals' faces because all things glorify God.
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r6.anchor: عن عمر رضي الله عنه قال: لا تلطموا وجوه الدواب فإن كل شيء يسبح بحمده

DURR-FULL:v5p289/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r7.claim: The Prophet says to ride animals gently and leave them healthy, not use them as seats for roadside talk; some mounts may remember God more than their riders.
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r7.anchor: عن معاذ بن أنس رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنه مر على قوم وهم وقوف على دواب

DURR-FULL:v5p289/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r8.claim: At sunrise, all God's creatures glorify Him except Satan and the wealthy among the children of Adam.
DURR-FULL:v5p289/r8.anchor: عن عمرو بن عبسة رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ما تستقل الشمس فيبقى من خلق الله

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r1.claim: Whenever a servant glorifies God once, something among God's created things also glorifies Him.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r1.anchor: عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه قال: ما من عبد يسبح الله تسبيحة إلا سبح ما خلق الله من شيء

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r2.claim: The Prophet says that ants glorify God.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن النمل يسبحن

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r3.claim: A prophet burned an anthill after an ant bit him; God rebuked him for burning a community that glorified Him because of one ant.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: قرصت نملة نبيا من الأنبياء

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r4.claim: The Prophet forbade killing frogs and said their croaking is glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قتل الضفدع وقال: نعيقها تسبيح

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r5.claim: Crops glorify God and their reward goes to their owner; clothing glorifies and asks a believer to wash off its dirt.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: الزرع يسبح بحمده وأجره لصاحبه

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r6.speaker: أبو قبيل
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r6.claim: Crops glorify God, and the reward belongs to the person who planted them.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r6.anchor: عن أبي قبيل رضي الله عنه قال: الزرع يسبح وثوابه للذي زرع

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas exempts donkeys and dogs from the claim that everything glorifies God.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كل شيء يسبح بحمده إلا الحمار والكلب

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r8.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: الاسطوانة تسبح والشجرة تسبح

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r9.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r9.claim: Do not criticize an animal or clothing because everything glorifies God.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: لا يعيبن أحدكم دابته ولا ثوبه فإن كل شيء يسبح بحمده

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r10.claim: It was reported that the creaking of a door is its glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r10.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه قال: ذكر لنا أن صرير الباب تسبيحه

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r11.speaker: أبو غالب الشيباني
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r11.claim: The sea's sound is its glorification, and its waves are its prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r11.anchor: عن أبي غالب الشيباني رضي الله عنه قال: صوت البحر تسبيحه وأمواجه صلاته

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r12.speaker: النخعي
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r12.anchor: عن النخعي رضي الله عنه قال: الطعام تسبيح

DURR-FULL:v5p290/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r13.speaker: أبو بكر
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r13.claim: Seeing a large-winged crow, Abu Bakr said game is hunted and trees cut because creatures neglect glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p290/r13.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران رضي الله عنه قال: أتي أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه بغراب وافر الجناحين

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r1.claim: A report through al-Zuhri says game is hunted and trees or branches cut because glorification is neglected.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r1.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه سلم يقول: ما صيد من صيد ولا عضدت عضاة

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r2.claim: Game is caught or vegetation cut only because glorification has been neglected.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما صيد من صيد ولا وشج من وشج

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r3.claim: No bird or fish is hunted before it abandons its prescribed glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما صيد من طير في السماء ولا سمك

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r4.claim: Birds and fish are caught because they have neglected glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r4.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما أخذ طائر ولا حوت إلا بتضييع التسبيح

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r5.claim: Nothing is caught among birds and fish except through neglecting God's glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r5.anchor: عن مرثد بن أبي مرثد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا يصطاد شيء من الطير والحيتان

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r6.claim: No bird is caught on land or sea but because it neglected glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r6.anchor: من طريق يزيد بن مرثد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ما اصطيد طير في بر ولا بحر

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r7.claim: Animal and insect lifespans are tied to glorification; when it ends God takes their souls, and the Angel of Death has no role in taking them.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r7.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: آجال البهائم كلها وخشاش الأرض والنمل والبراغيث

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r8.claim: Everything in its original state that is destined to die glorifies God.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وأن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: ما من شيء في أصله الأول لن يموت

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r9.claim: Al-Suddi likewise says everything in its original state that will die glorifies God.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r9.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: ما من شيء في أصله الأول لن يموت

DURR-FULL:v5p291/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r10.claim: When a diner said the table was glorifying, al-Hasan rejected that and limited the claim to things in their original state.
DURR-FULL:v5p291/r10.anchor: عن ابن شوذب قال: جلس الحسن مع أصحابه على مائدة فقال بعضهم: هذه المائدة تسبح الآن فقال الحسن: كلا

DURR-FULL:v5p292/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r1.claim: Ibrahim says that food's own glorification is its tasbih.
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن إبراهيم قال الطعام تسبيح

DURR-FULL:v5p292/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r2.claim: He says not to kill frogs because their sounds are glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال: لا تقتلوا الضفادع فإن أصواتها تسبيح

DURR-FULL:v5p292/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r3.claim: A frog's praise surpassed David's; an angel had him listen, and David swore he had never praised God with those words.
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r3.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: ظن داود عليه السلام أن أحدا لم يمدح خالقه

DURR-FULL:v5p292/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r4.speaker: صدقة بن يسار
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r4.claim: When David wondered whether God valued a tiny creature, a small pearl rebuked his self-regard, saying it thanked God more in proportion to its gifts.
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r4.anchor: عن صدقة بن يسار رضي الله عنه قال: كان داود عليه السلام في محرابه فأبصر درة صغيرة

DURR-FULL:v5p292/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r5.claim: Hasan says the verse is as weighty as a thousand Torah verses, which enumerate mountains, trees, and other things glorifying God.
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r5.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: هذه الآية في التوراة كقدر ألف آية

DURR-FULL:v5p292/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r6.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r6.claim: David sought refuge from God's all-seeing knowledge in the sea, mountains, and earth; God told him to work from hope or fear, then a frog reminded him that 70,000 frogs praised God.
DURR-FULL:v5p292/r6.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب رضي الله عنه قال: كان داود عليه السلام يسمى النواح في كتاب الله

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r1.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r1.claim: The continuation says a frog told David that 70,000 frogs stood on one leg praising and sanctifying God while he thought he alone praised in that hour.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r1.anchor: يا داود إنك حدثت نفسك أنك قد سبحت في ساعة ليس يذكر الله فيها غيرك

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r2.claim: David prayed through the night, then a frog told him it had been more diligent because he had dozed.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: صلى داود عليه السلام ليلة حتى أصبح فلما أن أصبح وجد في نفسه غرورا

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r3.speaker: أبو موسى
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r3.claim: Abu Musa says he was told that nothing glorifies God more than the red worm.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r3.anchor: عن أبي بردة عن أبي موسى رضي الله عنه قال: بلغني أنه ليس شيء أكثر تسبيحا من هذه الدودة الحمراء

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r4.claim: The soil glorifies God, and it continues glorifying when a wall is built in it.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: التراب يسبح فإذا بني فيه الحائط سبح

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r5.claim: Sounds of creaking from a house, wood, or walls are glorification.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: إذا سمعت تغيضا من البيت أو من الخشب والجدر فهو تسبيح

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r6.speaker: خيثمة
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r6.claim: Abu al-Darda's cooking pot fell over and began glorifying God.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r6.anchor: عن خيثمة رضي الله عنه قال: كان أبو الدرداء يطبخ قدرا فوقعت على وجهها فعلت تسبح

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r7.speaker: سليمان بن المغيرة
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r7.claim: When Mutarrif glorified God at home, his household vessels glorified along with him.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r7.anchor: عن سليمان بن المغيرة قال: كان مطرف رضي الله عنه إذا دخل بيته فسبح سبحت معه آنية بيته

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r8.claim: People could not remain settled if God's glorification in household objects were not veiled from them.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r8.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: لولا ما غمي عليكم من تسبيح ما معكم في البيوت ما تقاررتم

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r9.speaker: مسعر
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r9.claim: People could not remain settled if they were not veiled from the glorification of God's creation.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r9.anchor: عن مسعر رضي الله عنه قال: لولا ما غمي عليكم من تسبيح خلقه ما تقاررتم

DURR-FULL:v5p293/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r10.claim: Hasan restricts the verse's claim to every thing that has a soul.
DURR-FULL:v5p293/r10.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: كل شيء فيه الروح يسبح

DURR-FULL:v5p294/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies creation's prayer as its glorification: saying, Glory be to God and praise be to Him.
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: صلاة الخلق تسبيحهم سبحان الله وبحمده

DURR-FULL:v5p294/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r2.claim: The Prophet miraculously supplied water from his fingers; Ibn Masud says the companions heard its sound and glorification as they drank.
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله: كنا نسمع صوت الماء وتسبيحه وهو يشرب

DURR-FULL:v5p294/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says the companions heard the food glorifying as they ate with the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: كنا نأكل مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فنسمع تسبيح الطعام وهو يؤكل

DURR-FULL:v5p294/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r4.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r4.claim: The Prophet said a serving of thareed glorified, and several people heard it; he ordered it returned when a man asked that all hear it.
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r4.anchor: عن أنس قال: آتي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بطعام ثريد فقال: إن هذا الطعام يسبح

DURR-FULL:v5p294/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r5.speaker: محمد بن علي بن الحسين
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r5.claim: Muhammad al-Baqir says birds glorify their Lord and ask Him for that day's provision.
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r5.anchor: عن أبي حمزة الثمالي قال: قال محمد بن علي بن الحسين رضي الله عنه وسمع عصافير يصحن

DURR-FULL:v5p294/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r6.claim: Ali taught that birds praise their Lord at daybreak and ask Him for their daily provision; Ali Zayn al-Abidin disclaims knowledge of the unseen before relaying it.
DURR-FULL:v5p294/r6.anchor: سمعت أبي يقول: سمعت علي بن أبي طالب أمير المؤمنين رضي الله عنه يقول: إن الطير إذا أصبحت سبحت ربها

DURR-FULL:v5p295/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p295/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v5p295/r1.claim: Aisha reports that clothing glorifies God and becomes soiled enough for its glorification to cease, so the Prophet told her to wash two garments.
DURR-FULL:v5p295/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: دخل علي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال لي: يا عائشة اغسلي هذين البردين

DURR-FULL:v5p295/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p295/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p295/r2.claim: Qatada explains that God is forbearing toward creation and does not hasten as people may hasten against one another; He forgives them when they return.
DURR-FULL:v5p295/r2.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {إنه كان حليما غفورا} قال: حليما عن خلقه فلا يعجل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r1.claim: The clause about the worlds glorifying God is circumstantial to سبحانه: all created realms testify to His transcendence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r1.anchor: جملة { يسبح له } الخ . حال من الضمير في { سبحانه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r2.claim: The lām in له either marks transitivity of تسبيح understood as bearing witness to transcendence, or is the clarifying lām found in constructions such as الحمد لله لك.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r2.anchor: واللام في قوله : { له } لام تعدية { يسبح } المضمن معنى يشهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r3.claim: Since many things that cannot speak are said to glorify, their tasbīḥ means that their state points to God's transcendence; people fail to understand because they neglect to observe that evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r3.anchor: دل على أنه مستعمل في الدلالة على التنزيه بدلالة الحال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r4.claim: The address لا تفقهون may target pagans who deny the transcendence creation displays, while believers can perceive it through Quran-guided reflection; alternatively, it addresses everyone because no one fully comprehends this glorification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r4.anchor: والخطاب في { لا تفقهون } يجوز أن يكون للمشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r5.speaker: فخر الدين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r5.claim: Fakhr al-Din illustrates the point with an apple: each indivisible part and its specific qualities indicate a wise, powerful determiner, while their countless parts and qualities remain unknown to us.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p114#3/r5.anchor: وقد مثل الإمام فخر الدين ذلك فقال : إنك إذا أخذت تفاحة واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r1.claim: Choosing تفقهون rather than تعلمون suggests that the denied knowledge is subtle and detailed, supporting Fakhr al-Din's argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r1.anchor: ولعل إيثار فعل { لا تفقهون } دون أن يقول : لا تعلمون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r2.claim: These readers recite يسبح with feminine plural تاء; both it and the masculine singular are permitted with non-rational plurals and nonliteral feminine nouns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r2.anchor: وقرأه أبو عمرو ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم ، ويعقوب ، وخلف بتاء جماعة المؤنث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r3.claim: God's forbearance and forgiveness imply that the pagans' claim would otherwise merit swift worldly punishment; the verse urges them to desist so they may be forgiven.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r3.anchor: تعريض بأن مقالتهم تقتضي تعجيل العقاب لهم في الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r4.claim: The added كان presents forbearance and forgiveness as established, enduring attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p115/r4.anchor: وزيادة ( كان ) للدلالة على أن الحلم والغفران صفتان له محققتان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r8.claim: The heavens, earth, and their inhabitants declare God above the partners attributed to Him; “those in them” includes angels, humans, and jinn, and every thing praises and glorifies Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r8.anchor: المعنى ينزهه عن هذه المقالة التي لكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r9.claim: The pronoun treating the heavens and earth as rational reflects that they perform the rational action of glorifying God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r9.anchor: ثم أعاد على السماوات والأرض ضمير من يعقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459/r10.claim: Some scholars take universal glorification figuratively: created things reveal their Maker, and this sight prompts the reflective observer to glorify Him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r1.claim: Another group limits the general wording to living or growing things; Ikrima says a tree glorifies God, whereas a column does not.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r1.anchor: وقالت فرقة من شيء لفظ عموم، ومعناه الخصوص في كل حي ونام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r2.speaker: يزيد الرقاشي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r2.claim: Yazid al-Raqqashi says a dining tray once glorified God when it was a living, growing tree; after becoming a coated inanimate object, it did not.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r2.anchor: وقال يزيد الرقاشي للحسن وهما في طعام، وقد قدم الخوان: أيسبح هذا الخوان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r3.claim: A third group takes the wording literally and universally: every thing glorifies God in a manner humans neither hear nor comprehend; Ibn Atiyya answers that not understanding may describe heedless disbelievers who ignore the lesson in creation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan reports that the Torah lists a thousand examples of creation glorifying God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: بلغني أن معنى هذه الآية في التوراة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r5.claim: Readings vary between yusbbiḥu and tusabbiḥu, both of which Ibn Atiyya accepts; Ibn Mas'ud, Talha, and al-A'mash read “the heavens glorified.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r5.anchor: والقراءتان حسنتان، وقرأ عبد الله بن مسعود وطلحة والأعمش «سبحت له السماوات»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r6.claim: The closing names remind hearers that God patiently delays and pardons them despite their grave attribution, which every creature repudiates.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p459#2/r6.anchor: إنه كان حليما غفورا فلذلك أمهلكم

SULAMI:v1p388#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p388#3/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
SULAMI:v1p388#3/r1.claim: Abu Uthman al-Maghribi says all created things glorify God in different languages, but only God-knowing scholars with opened hearts' ears hear and understand it.
SULAMI:v1p388#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان المغربي : المكونات كلهن يسبحن الله باختلاف اللغات ، ولكن لا يسمع تسبيحها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r1.claim: They read the verb tasbaḥ with feminine tāʾ; other readers use masculine yāʾ, which al-Farrāʾ says suits a small number of feminine or masculine subjects.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم تسبح بالتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r2.speaker: العلماء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r2.claim: The heavens' glorification is evidence that God is the Creator and powerful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r2.anchor: قال العلماء والمراد بهذا التسبيح الدلالة على أنه الخالق القادر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r3.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r3.claim: One view takes the universal wording literally: everything glorifies God, even clothing, food, and a door's creaking.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r3.anchor: أنه على إطلاقه فكل شيء يسبحه حتى الثوب والطعام وصرير الباب قاله إبراهيم النخعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r4.claim: One restricted interpretation says all living things glorify God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r4.anchor: أنه كل شيء فيه الروح قاله الحسن وقتادة والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r5.claim: Another restriction includes living beings and growing plants: a tree glorifies, but a column does not; al-Hasan once said a serving tray used to glorify.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r6.speaker: خالد بن معدان عن المقدام بن معدي كرب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r6.claim: A report says dust glorifies until wet, a leaf while on its tree, and new clothing until it becomes dirty; each ceases when altered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r6.anchor: إن التراب ليسبح ما لم يبتل فاذا ابتل ترك التسبيح وإن الورقة تسبح ما دامت على الشجرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r7.claim: Speaking animals' glorification is known; non-speaking animals may glorify by sound or by indicating their Maker.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r7.anchor: فأما تسبيح الحيوان الناطق فمعلوم وتسبيح الحيوان غير الناطق فجائز ان يكون بصوته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r8.claim: Three views of inanimate glorification are that it is real but known only to God, submission to God, or its pointing to its Maker and thus prompting an observer to glorify.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r8.anchor: وفي تسبيح الجمادات ثلاثة أقوال أحدها انه تسبيح لا يعلمه الا الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r9.claim: If glorification is literal, the statement that people do not understand it addresses all people; if it means evidence of the Maker, it addresses disbelievers who fail to infer and reflect.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r9.anchor: فان قلنا إنه تسبيح حقيقة كان قوله ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم لجميع الخلق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r10.claim: The meanings of Forbearing and Forgiving were explained at al-Baqara 225.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p39/r10.anchor: وقد شرحنا معنى الحليم و الغفور في البقرة 225

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p78#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p78#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p78#3/r1.claim: The seven heavens, earth, and all creatures glorify, exalt, and declare God’s oneness in lordship and divinity, in contrast to the polytheists’ claims; Ibn Kathir cites 19:90–92 about creation nearly breaking over the claim of a divine child.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p78#3/r1.anchor: تقدسه السموات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن، أي: من المخلوقات، وتنزهه وتعظمه وتجله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p78#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p78#3/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن قرط
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p78#3/r2.claim: A report about the Night Journey says the Prophet heard the highest heavens glorifying God with praise while returning from Jerusalem; Ibn Kathir gives no grading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p78#3/r2.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن قرط؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة أسري إلى المسجد الأقصى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r1.claim: Every created thing glorifies God, but people do not understand its praise because it is in a language unlike theirs; the more famous of two views includes animals, plants, and inanimate things.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r1.anchor: وهذا عام في الحيوانات (5) والنبات والجماد، وهذا أشهر القولين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud says they heard food glorifying while it was being eaten; the report is in Sahih al-Bukhari.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه قال: كنا نسمع تسبيح الطعام وهو يؤكل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r3.claim: A well-known report says the Prophet and then Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman heard pebbles in their hands glorifying like bees humming.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r3.anchor: أن النبي (7) صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ في يده حصيات، فسمع لهن تسبيح كحنين النحل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r4.claim: The Prophet tells people not to overburden mounts or use them as seats for roadside conversations, since some mounts remember God more than their riders.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r4.anchor: فقال لهم: "اركبوها سالمة، ودعوها سالمة، ولا تتخذوها كراسي لأحاديثكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r5.claim: A report in al-Nasaʾi says the Prophet forbade killing frogs because their croaking is glorification.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r5.anchor: وفي سنن النسائي عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قتل الضفدع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r6.claim: Qatada transmits from ʿAbd Allah ibn Babi, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, that basic declarations of faith, praise, greatness, glorification, and reliance are forms of creation’s prayer and praise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة، عن عبد الله بن بابي (12) ، عن عبد الله بن عمرو: أن الرجل إذا قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r7.claim: A report tells of an Arab criticizing the Prophet for raising a low-status shepherd and lowering a nobleman; the Prophet rebukes his brocade clothing and recounts Noah’s counsel to avoid shirk and pride and to say the two glorifications, which are creation’s prayer and source of provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p79/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعرابي عليه جبة من طيالسة مكفوفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r1.claim: Ahmad transmits a longer version of Noah’s counsel to his sons about avoiding shirk and pride and saying the testimony of faith and God’s praise; Ibn Kathir says this transmission is unique.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r1.anchor: ورواه الإمام أحمد، أيضا، عن سليمان بن حرب، عن حماد بن زيد، عن الصقعب (5) بن زهير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r2.claim: A report from Jabir says Noah told his son that glorifying God is creation’s prayer and means of provision; Ibn Jarir links it to this verse but Ibn Kathir notes its chain is weak because Musa ibn ʿUbayda is weak to most critics.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله، رضي الله عنه (7) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ألا أخبركم بشيء أمر به نوح ابنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r3.claim: Ikrima says columns and trees glorify; some early authorities add that a door’s creaking and flowing water are their glorification.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة في قوله تعالى: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: الأسطوانة تسبح، والشجرة تسبح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r4.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri transmits from Mansur that Ibrahim said food glorifies; Ibn Kathir says the prostration verse at the start of Surat al-Hajj supports this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r4.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري، عن منصور، عن إبراهيم قال: الطعام يسبح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r5.claim: Another view restricts glorification to beings with life: Qatada includes anything with a spirit, such as a tree, and al-Hasan and al-Dahhak say the same.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال: كل شيء فيه الروح يسبح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r6.claim: In a report about a wooden table, al-Hasan says it used to glorify; Ibn Kathir infers that it did so while alive and green but stopped when cut and dry.
