IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r6.anchor: فقدموا الخوان، فقال يزيد الرقاشي: يا أبا سعيد، يسبح هذا الخوان؟ فقال: كان يسبح مرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r7.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says two grave-dwellers were punished for failing to guard against urine and for carrying tales; the Prophet placed moist palm branches on their graves hoping their punishment would lessen until they dried.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p80/r7.anchor: ثم أخذ جريدة رطبة، فشقها نصفين، ثم غرز في كل قبر واحدة، ثم قال: "لعله يخفف عنهما ما لم ييبسا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r1.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r1.claim: Some scholars explain the palm branches’ effect as their glorification while green and moist, which ends when they dry; Ibn Kathir leaves the matter to God’s knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r1.anchor: قال بعض من تكلم على هذا الحديث من العلماء: إنما قال: "ما لم ييبسا" لأنهما يسبحان ما دام فيهما خضرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r2.claim: God is forbearing and forgiving: He delays punishment for sinners, but takes those who persist in disbelief and defiance; those who abandon sin and repent receive forgiveness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r2.anchor: أي: إنه [تعالى] (6) لا يعاجل من عصاه بالعقوبة، بل يؤجله وينظره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r3.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says God gives an oppressor respite until He seizes him and does not let him escape; the Prophet then recites 11:102.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r3.anchor: كما جاء في الصحيحين: "إن الله ليملي للظالم، حتى إذا أخذه لم يفلته". ثم قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir links this ending to 35:41–45: God alone holds the heavens and earth, and delays judgment to a fixed term rather than destroying every creature for its deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p81/r4.anchor: كما قال في آخر فاطر: {إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا ولئن زالتا

JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir reads all three verbs with yāʾ, reporting the polytheists' words in the first two and using masculine agreement in the third.
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r3.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ثلاثة بالياء: (لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون)

JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف بن هشام
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r4.claim: They use direct address with tāʾ for the first two forms and feminine agreement for the heavens in the third.
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r4.anchor: وقراءة حمزة والكسائي وخلف بن هشام، كلها بالتاء في الأولين

JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r5.claim: They use direct address in the first verb, narration in the second, and masculine agreement in the third because another element intervenes.
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم في الأولى بالتاء

JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r6.claim: They address listeners with tāʾ in the first verb, narrate with yāʾ in the second, and use feminine agreement for the heavens in the third.
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ويعقوب الأولى بالتاء، أي: قل لهم: لو كان معه آلهة كما تقولون،

JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r7.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r7.claim: Hafs reads the first two verbs with yāʾ and “the heavens glorify” with feminine tāʾ.
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم: كما يقولون وعما يقولون بالياء على الحكاية،

JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4213#2/r9.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring transcendence; ʿuluww is used as a verbal noun for taʿāliyā.

JISHUMI:v6p4215/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r1.claim: Fiqh generally means knowledge, but convention restricts it to religious law requiring inference; thus God is not called a faqīh.

JISHUMI:v6p4215/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r2.claim: Ḥalīm means forbearing, the opposite of foolishness.
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r2.anchor: والحليم: من الحلم فعيل بمعنى فاعل، وضده: السفيه.

JISHUMI:v6p4215/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r4.claim: Ḥalīman is accusative as the predicate of kāna.

JISHUMI:v6p4215/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r5.claim: One coherence reading attaches “forbearing, forgiving” to “transcendent.”
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r5.anchor: أحدهما: أنه راجع إلى قوله: سبحانه أي: سبحان الحليم الغفور،

JISHUMI:v6p4215/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r6.claim: Another reading says God gives respite and blessings despite lies, then forgives those who repent.
JISHUMI:v6p4215/r6.anchor: يمهلهم مع كذبهم وينعم عليهم مع إصرارهم، ثم يغفر لهم إذا تابوا،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r1.claim: The heavens, earth, and their contents glorify God through testimony of their state, demonstrating their Maker, power, and wisdom and declaring Him free of partners.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r1.anchor: والمراد أنها تسبح له بلسان الحال ، حيث تدل على الصانع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r2.claim: The address targets polytheists: associating partners while affirming God as Creator shows they failed to consider the evidence. Figurative glorification applies to all creation; otherwise a word would be literal and figurative at once.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r2.anchor: الخطاب للمشركين ، وهم وإن كانوا إذا سئلوا عن خالق السموات والأرض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r3.claim: God's forbearance and forgiveness appear in delaying punishment despite heedlessness, bad reasoning, failure to understand the signs, and shirk.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p626#2/r3.anchor: حين لا يعاجلكم بالعقوبة على غفلتكم وسوء نظركم

FARRA:v2p123/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p123/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p123/r8.claim: Most readers use feminine تسبح; ʿAbd Allāh’s reading سبحت supports tāʾ, although masculine agreement would also be valid for a small-number collective.
FARRA:v2p123/r8.anchor: أكثر القراء على التاء. وهي في قراءة عبد الله (سبحت له السموات السبع)

FARRA:v2p123/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p123/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p123/r9.claim: With a small count, masculine agreement may be preferable; when the verb precedes, the visible subject leaves the verb in yāʾ form, while feminine agreement can reflect the understood هذه.
FARRA:v2p123/r9.anchor: و (يكاد) وإنما حسنت الياء لأنه عدد قليل، وإذا قل العدد من المؤنث والمذكر

FARRA:v2p123/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p123/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
FARRA:v2p123/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says every tasbīḥ in the Qur’an is prayer and every sulṭān is proof, citing that all things glorify God.
FARRA:v2p123/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: كل تسبيح في القرآن فهو صلاة، وكل سلطان حجة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r1.claim: Only living things glorify God; nonliving things do not.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r1.anchor: فأما ما ليس بحي فلا , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r2.claim: Every created thing, living or not—even a door's creak—glorifies God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, creation's subtle workmanship and wondrous power, beyond human imitation, prompt observers to glorify and sanctify God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r3.anchor: لطيف صنعته وبديع قدرته الذي يعجز الخلق عن مثله

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r4.claim: An unnamed poet depicts creation's beauty prompting praise wherever the observer turns, supporting the sign-based interpretation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p245#2/r4.anchor: كما قال الشاعر : تلقي بتسبيحة من حيثما انصرفت

MUQATIL:17:44-45/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r1.claim: All seven heavens, earth, and everything in them remember and glorify God by His command, including plants, animals, and other created things; people do not hear their praise.
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r1.anchor: يعني تذكره، { السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن وإن من شيء } ، يعني وما من شىء

MUQATIL:17:44-45/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r2.claim: The thunder's glorification is likewise by God's command, as is the praise of plants and creatures.
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r2.anchor: يعني بأمره، من نبت، أو دابة، أو خلق

MUQATIL:17:44-45/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r3.claim: God is forbearing and forgiving toward the polytheists: He overlooks their claims that He has partners and delays their punishment until its appointed time.
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r3.anchor: حين لا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة، { غفورا } في تأخير العذاب عنهم إلى المدة

MUQATIL:17:44-45/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r4.claim: God's preservation of the heavens and earth from vanishing is another parallel concerning His forbearance.
MUQATIL:17:44-45/r4.anchor: إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r1.claim: Iraqi readers other than Abu Bakr read تسبيح with the feminine تاء.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r2.claim: Every thing glorifies by saying Glory be to God and praise be to Him.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r3.speaker: السدي عن النبي
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi transmits a Prophetic report that no fish is caught or bird flies except in connection with what is lost of God's glorification.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r3.anchor: عن السدى قال عليه السلام ما اصطيد حوت في البحر ولا طائر يطير إلا بما يضيع من تسبيح الله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r4.claim: People fail to understand creation's glorification either because its languages differ or because perception is difficult; another explanation is that it prompts the observer to praise, and one who guides to good shares its reward. The first explanation is preferred.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r4.anchor: لاختلاف اللغات أو لتعسر الادراك أو سبب لتسبيح الناظر أليه والدال على الخير كفاعله والوجه الأول

NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r5.claim: God is forbearing toward servants' ignorance and forgives believers' sins.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p288#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ إنه كان حليما ﴾ عن جهل العباد ﴿ غفورا ﴾ لذنوب المؤمنين

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r1.claim: The heavens and earth use a rational pronoun because they are assigned praise; those within them are angels, humans, and jinn before the verse broadens to every thing.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r1.anchor: أعاد على السموات والأرض ضمير من يعقل، لما أسند إليها فعل العاقل وهو التسبيح.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r2.speaker: some scholars
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r2.claim: One group takes praise as signs that created things testify God is Creator; another takes it literally and inaudibly, with a reply that disbelievers fail to reflect on God's wisdom.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r2.anchor: فقالت فرقة: ليس مخصوصا والمراد به تسبيح الدلالة، وكل محدث يشهد على نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r3.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r3.claim: A third group limits praise to living things; ʿIkrima says a tree praises but a pillar does not. Al-Hasan says a table once praised when it was a tree.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r3.anchor: ومن هذا قول عكرمة: الشجرة تسبح والأسطوان لا يسبح.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet passed two punished graves, identified backbiting and failure to avoid urine, and placed fresh palm branches there hoping for relief until they dried.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44/r4.anchor: ويستدل لهذا القول من السنة بما ثبت عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r1.claim: Scholars infer planting trees and reciting Qur'an at graves can benefit the dead; Qurtubi says dedicated Qur'anic reward reaches them. Alternatively every animate and inanimate thing praises.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r1.anchor: قال علماؤنا: ويستفاد من هذا غرس الأشجار وقراءة القرآن على القبور

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r2.claim: Qurtubi cites David's mountains praising, stones falling in fear according to Mujahid, and mountains nearly rupturing when people attribute a child to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r2.anchor: واذكر عبدنا داوود ذا الأيد إنه أواب إنا سخرنا الجبال معه يسبحن بالعشي والإشراق

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud says mountains ask whether someone remembered God; Anas says regions of earth ask each other morning and evening. The Prophet says creatures hearing the call to prayer will testify.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r3.anchor:
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لا يسمع صوت المؤذن جن ولا إنس ولا شجر ولا حجر

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r4.speaker: جابر بن سمرة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r4.claim: Jabir ibn Samura reports a Meccan stone greeted the Prophet before his mission; Qurtubi says it may have been the Black Stone.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#2/r4.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن جابر بن سمرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r1.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r1.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi says all things, living and inanimate, praise—even a door's creak; an alternative says inanimate things prompt observers to glorify their creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r1.anchor: وكذا قال النخعي وغيره: هو عام فيما فيه روح وفيما لا روح فيه حتى صرير الباب.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r2.claim: Qurtubi prefers literal praise by everything, supported by reports and Qur'anic wording; otherwise David's special mention would be unexplained. God creates life and speech in things to praise Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r2.anchor: فالصحيح أن الكل يسبح للأخبار الدالة على ذلك ولو كان ذلك التسبيح تسبيح دلالة فأي تخصيص لداود

QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r3.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وحفص وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r3.claim: These readers use feminine ta-yafqahuna; others read masculine ya, which Abu ʿUbayd chooses because of an intervening word. God is forbearing in this life and forgiving believers in the next.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:44#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وحفص وحمزة والكسائي وخلف «تفقهون» بالتاء لتأنيث الفاعل.

RAZI-FULL:v20p173#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p173#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p173#2/r5.claim: The readings of the pronouns differ: Ibn Kathir reads all three in third person; Hamza and al-Kisa'i use second person throughout; Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Abu Bakr vary them; Hafs reads the first two third person and the last second person; Abu Amr the first and last second person, middle third.
RAZI-FULL:v20p173#2/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير كما يقولون وعما يقولون ويسبح بالياء في هذه الثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v20p174/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p174/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p174/r4.claim: Living, accountable beings glorify God verbally and by displaying His unity and perfection; animals and inanimate objects can only glorify through the latter evidence, since speech-based praise requires understanding and life.
RAZI-FULL:v20p174/r4.anchor: فأما الذي لا يكون مكلفا مثل البهائم ، ومن

RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r1.claim: Allowing inert matter to know and speak would undermine the proof that knowledge and power entail life, contrary to the necessary truth that what is not alive cannot know, act, or speak; he says recognized scholars uphold this.
RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r1.anchor: أن من ليس بحي لم يكن عالما قادرا متكلما

RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r2.claim: Some argue that animals, plants, and inert objects literally praise God: because people cannot understand their praise, it must be distinct from their evident testimony to divine power and wisdom.

RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p175/r3.claim: Answering this, Razi says every indivisible part of an apple, and each contingent feature assigned to it, independently testifies to a wise, powerful creator; their uncounted parts and features explain why people do not comprehend this praise.

RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r1.claim: A second answer is that polytheists professed a creator but did not contemplate the signs around them, so they failed to grasp the world's testimony to God.
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r1.anchor: كانوا يقرون بألسنتهم بإثبات إله العالم إلا أنهم ما كانوا يتفكرون

RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r2.claim: A third answer is that they did not recognize God's full power, doubted resurrection, and missed the proof from mutual hindrance; the heavens and earth attest to that proof.
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r2.anchor: استبعدوا كونه تعالى قادرا على الحشر والنشر

RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r3.claim: More broadly, they overlooked most proofs of divine unity, justice, prophecy, and resurrection; calling this ignorance a grave fault and pairing it with God's forbearance and forgiveness suits failure to recognize evidence, not inaudible verbal praise.
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r3.anchor: ذكر الحليم والغفور ههنا يدل على أن كونهم بحيث لا يفقهون

RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r4.claim: The literal-praise view is inconsistent: its advocates say slaughter stops an animal's praise and breaking stops a branch's, although being inanimate supposedly does not prevent praise.
RAZI-FULL:v20p175#2/r4.anchor: صار ذبح الحيوان مانعا له من التسبيح

RAZI-FULL:v20p176/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p176/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p176/r1.claim: Because the verse includes both rational beings who literally say 'glory be to God' and inanimate things whose state signifies God's transcendence, the same verb would be literal and metaphorical at once, which legal theory rejects; Razi therefore takes it metaphorically for inanimate things.
RAZI-FULL:v20p176/r1.anchor: فالأولى أن يحمل هذا التسبيح على الوجه المجازي في حق الجمادات

NAHHAS:v2p425/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p425/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p425/r5.claim: The feminine verb تسبح agrees with the feminine plural group; يسبح is also used with masculine agreement for the whole group.
NAHHAS:v2p425/r5.anchor: على تأنيث الجماعة ويسبح على تذكير الجميع

NAHHAS:v2p425/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p425/r6.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v2p425/r6.claim: Some scholars take every created thing's tasbīḥ as familiar, actual glorification.
NAHHAS:v2p425/r6.anchor: فقال بعضهم : هو التسبيح الذي يعرف

NAHHAS:v2p425/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p425/r7.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v2p425/r7.claim: Another scholarly view restricts the meaning of the universal tasbīḥ, without further specification here.

NAHHAS:v2p425/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p425/r8.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v2p425/r8.claim: A third view says creation's tasbīḥ consists in its indicating God's transcendence.
NAHHAS:v2p425/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : تسبيحه دلالته على تنزيه الله جل وعز

NAHHAS:v2p425/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p425/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p425/r9.claim: One interpretation addresses unbelievers who fail to infer God's transcendence; another addresses people generally because some cannot comprehend creation's tasbīḥ.
NAHHAS:v2p425/r9.anchor: على أنه مخاطبة للكفار الذين لا يستدلون

NAHHAS:v2p425/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p425/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p425/r10.claim: God is forbearing toward those who fail to infer, and forgiving toward those who repent.
NAHHAS:v2p425/r10.anchor: أي حليما عن هؤلاء الذين لا يستدلون ^ ( غفورا ) ^ لمن تاب منهم

STUDYQURAN:17:44/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r1.claim: All creatures, including angels, beasts, and inanimate things, worship and praise God; the verse links to other descriptions of creation praising or prostrating to Him.
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r1.anchor: God is worshipped by all creatures in existence—both those on earth and those in heaven, angels as well as beasts, and even inanimate creatures

STUDYQURAN:17:44/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r2.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r2.claim: The verse continues verse 42: all created things are subordinate to their Creator and turn toward Him, so worshipping them ignores their dependence; their contingency points to the necessary, uncreated Creator.
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r2.anchor: the contingency of all these phenomena that points to the existence of the one uncreated Creator, who is necessary in Himself

STUDYQURAN:17:44/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r3.claim: Some understand Glory be to Him as the universal prayer of all creatures despite their praise transcending human understanding.
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r3.anchor: some have considered Glory be to Him (as in v. 43) to be the universal prayer of all creatures

STUDYQURAN:17:44/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r4.claim: Some commentators say people should never disrespect animals or any creature, since they possess spirit and praise God.
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r4.anchor: one should never show disrespect to any animal, or indeed to any creature, for they too are possessed of spirit and praise God

STUDYQURAN:17:44/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r5.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r5.claim: God is Clement because He delays punishment of wrongdoers; He is Forgiving toward those seeking His forgiveness.
STUDYQURAN:17:44/r5.anchor: God is Clement, in that He does not bring punishment down upon wrongdoers immediately

TAB-FULL:v14p604/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p604/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p604/r4.claim: The seven heavens, earth, and their inhabitants glorify God to exalt and revere Him; the inhabitants include believers among angels, humans, and jinn.
TAB-FULL:v14p604/r4.anchor: تنزه الله أيها المشركون عما وصفتموه به إعظاما له وإجلالا، السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن من المؤمنين به من الملائكة والإنس والجن

TAB-FULL:v14p607/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r1.anchor: وما من شيء من خلقه إلا يسبح بحمده

TAB-FULL:v14p607/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r2.claim: The Prophet recounts Noah's instruction to his son to glorify God, calling it creation's prayer and glorification and a means of provision.
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ألا أخبركم بشيء أمر به نوح ابنه؟ إن نوحا قال لابنه يا بني آمرك أن تقول سبحان الله وبحمده

TAB-FULL:v14p607/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r3.claim: Ikrima says not to insult an animal or garment because everything glorifies God.
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r3.anchor: سمعت عكرمة، يقول: لا يعيبن أحدكم دابته ولا ثوبه

TAB-FULL:v14p607/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r4.claim: Ikrima says trees and columns glorify God.
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة، {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} [الإسراء: 44] قال: الشجرة تسبح، والأسطوانة تسبح

TAB-FULL:v14p607/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r5.claim: When asked whether a serving tray glorifies God, al-Hasan replied that it used to glorify.
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r5.anchor: قال يزيد الرقاشي: يا أبا سعيد يسبح هذا الخوان: فقال: كان يسبح مرة

TAB-FULL:v14p607/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r6.speaker: الضحاك والحسن
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Hasan say everything possessing a spirit glorifies God.
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك، ويونس، عن الحسن، أنهما قالا في قوله: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} [الإسراء: 44] قالا: كل شيء فيه الروح

TAB-FULL:v14p607/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r7.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم، قال: الطعام يسبح

TAB-FULL:v14p607/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r8.claim: Qatada says every living thing, including trees and other beings with life, glorifies God.
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} [الإسراء: 44] قال: كل شيء فيه الروح يسبح، من شجر أو شيء فيه الروح

TAB-FULL:v14p607/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r9.claim: A report from Abd Allah ibn Amr explains the virtues of remembrance: profession is sincerity, praise is thanks, “God is greatest” fills heaven and earth, glorification is creation's prayer, and the final phrase expresses submission.
TAB-FULL:v14p607/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي، عن عبد الله بن عمرو، أن الرجل، إذا قال: لا إله إلا الله فهي كلمة الإخلاص

TAB-FULL:v14p607#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p607#2/r1.claim: God forgives people's sins when they repent, covering them with His pardon.
TAB-FULL:v14p607#2/r1.anchor: والأنداد بالعقوبة. {غفورا} [النساء: 23] يقول: ساترا ذنوبهم، إذا هم تابوا منها بالعفو منه لهم

TAB-FULL:v14p607#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p607#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p607#2/r2.claim: Qatada says God does not hasten as some people do and forgives people when they repent.
TAB-FULL:v14p607#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {إنه كان حليما} [الإسراء: 44] عن خلقه، فلا يعجل كعجلة بعضهم على بعض {غفورا} [النساء: 23]

TABATABAI:17:43-44/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:43-44/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:43-44/r4.claim: The world’s glorification completes the preceding proof: all creation comes from God, depends on Him, returns to Him, and submits to Him, so no other being can own the kingdom or be a lord.
TABATABAI:17:43-44/r4.anchor: فإنها لم تبتدئ إلا منه ولا تنتهي إلا إليه ولا تقوم إلا به ولا تخضع سجدا إلا له

TABATABAI:17:44/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:44/r1.claim: Tasbīḥ is verbal disclosure of what is within, but speech need not use human words or audible sounds; any sign that reveals a meaning can be speech, as Quran also calls God’s nonhuman disclosure speech.
TABATABAI:17:44/r1.anchor: حقيقه الكلام الكشف عما في الضمير بنوع من الإشاره إليه والدلاله عليه

TABATABAI:17:44/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:44/r2.claim: Heaven, earth, and their inhabitants truly glorify God: their dependence and deficiencies disclose their self-sufficient, perfect Creator, while the integrated order of creation reveals one source and governor.
TABATABAI:17:44/r2.anchor: ليست لها في أنفسها إلا محض الحاجه وصرف الفاقة إليه في ذاتها وصفاتها وأحوالها

TABATABAI:17:44/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:44/r3.claim: The meaning and words a denier uses, and all the means used to communicate them, are themselves dependent created things that testify to one God.
TABATABAI:17:44/r3.anchor: فإن المعنى الذي تصور في ضمير هذا الإنسان واللفظ الذي يلفظه لسانه

TABATABAI:17:44#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:44#2/r1.claim: Tasbīḥ in all beings is literal conscious speech, not mere metaphorical evidence: knowledge accompanies creation in proportion to existence, so each created thing senses itself and manifests its dependence on its Lord.
TABATABAI:17:44#2/r1.anchor: كلامه تعالى مشعر بأن العلم سار في الموجودات مع سريان الخلقه فلكل منها حظ من العلم

TABATABAI:17:44#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:44#2/r2.claim: The author rejects both treating inanimate glorification as figurative signs and dividing tasbīḥ into real speech for living beings but metaphorical state for others; all things speak truly without human phonemes.
TABATABAI:17:44#2/r2.anchor: والحق أن التسبيح في الجميع حقيقي قالي غير أن كونه قاليا لا يستلزم أن يكون بألفاظ موضوعة

TABATABAI:17:44-45/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44-45/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:44-45/r1.claim: The verse extends tasbīḥ from the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants to every thing, adding praise: need and deficiency reveal God’s transcendence, while existence and gifted beauty praise His acts and attributes.
TABATABAI:17:44-45/r1.anchor: فتفيد أن كل شيء كما يسبحه تعالى كذلك يحمده بالثناء عليه بجميل صفاته وأفعاله

TABATABAI:17:44-45/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44-45/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:44-45/r2.claim: ‘You do not understand their glorification’ shows conscious, literal praise, not mere evidence of a creator, which people already grasp; proposed excuses about heedless polytheists or partial understanding do not fit the proof’s context.
TABATABAI:17:44-45/r2.anchor: وهم على أي حال يفقهون دلالة الأشياء على صانعها مع أن الآية تنفي عنهم الفقه

TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r1.claim: David’s mountains and birds glorify, and traditions from Shiʿi and Sunni routes report objects, including pebbles in the Prophet’s hand, praising God; these contexts preclude merely figurative reading.
TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r1.anchor: إنا سخرنا الجبال معه يسبحن بالعشي والإشراق

TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r2.claim: God is forbearing and forgiving: He delays punishment and forgives the repentant; these attributes show that His sovereignty cannot be diminished and mercy causes Him no harm.
TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r2.anchor: يمهل فلا يعاجل بالعقوبة ويغفر من تاب ورجع إليه

TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r3.claim: A cited explanation says people deserve punishment for failing to understand all creation’s continual glorification, but God’s forbearance and forgiveness spare them; the author calls this a good explanation without requiring that humans can fully understand it.
TABATABAI:17:44-45#2/r3.anchor: وقد قيل في وجه هذا التذييل أنه إشاره إلى أن الإنسان في قصوره عن فهم هذا التسبيح

TABATABAI:17:55/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:55/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
TABATABAI:17:55/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet said Noah, near death, urged his sons to praise God, the prayer of everything by which everything receives provision.
TABATABAI:17:55/r6.anchor: أخرج أحمد وابن مردويه عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال أن نوحا لما حضرته الوفاه

TABATABAI:17:55/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:55/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:55/r7.claim: The link between universal praise and provision is that each being manifests its need, thereby indicating God's freedom from need.
TABATABAI:17:55/r7.anchor: فإن الرزق يقدر بالحاجه والسؤال وكل شيء إنما يسبح الله تعالى بالإشاره بإظهار حاجته

TABATABAI:17:55/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:55/r8.speaker: أبو الصباح
TABATABAI:17:55/r8.claim: Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ reports from Abū ʿAbd Allāh that every thing praises God and that a wall's cracking is its praise; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes another transmission through al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd.
TABATABAI:17:55/r8.anchor: في تفسير العياشي عن أبي الصباح عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قلت له قول الله { وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده }

TABATABAI:17:40-55/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r1.claim: The al-Nawfalī–al-Sakūnī report through Jaʿfar and his father says the Prophet prohibited branding animals and striking their faces because they praise their Lord.
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r1.anchor: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يوسم البهائم وأن يضرب وجهها فإنها تسبح بحمد ربها

TABATABAI:17:40-55/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r2.speaker: محمد بن مسلم
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r2.claim: A parallel al-Kāfī report through Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet, forbids striking an animal's face and says not to brand its face.
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r2.anchor: وروي النهي عن ضربها على وجوهها الكليني في الكافي بإسناده عن محمد بن مسلم

TABATABAI:17:40-55/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r3.speaker: إسحاق بن عمار
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r3.claim: Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār reports from Abū ʿAbd Allāh that birds and wild animals are caught only when their praise has been neglected.
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r3.anchor: وفيه عن إسحاق بن عمار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال ما من طير يصاد في بر أو بحر

TABATABAI:17:40-55/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r4.claim: The author notes that Sunnis transmit this teaching through Ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Abū Hurayra, and others from the Prophet.
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r4.anchor: وهذا المعنى رواه أهل السنة بطرق كثيرة عن ابن مسعود وأبي الدرداء وأبي هريره وغيرهم عن النبي

TABATABAI:17:40-55/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r5.speaker: مسعدة بن صدقة
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r5.claim: Musʿada ibn Ṣadaqa reports from Jaʿfar and his father that dry wood praises God: the cracking sound of house timber is its praise.
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r5.anchor: عن مسعده بن صدقة عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عليهما السلام أنه دخل عليه رجل

TABATABAI:17:40-55/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said ants praise God.
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r6.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي هريره أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

TABATABAI:17:40-55/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet prohibited killing frogs because their croaking is praise.
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال نهى رسول الله عن قتل الضفدع وقال نعيقها تسبيح

TABATABAI:17:40-55/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r8.speaker: أبو حمزة
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r8.claim: Abū Ḥamza reports that ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn relayed from his father and ʿAlī that birds praise God and ask for daily sustenance; another version gives this from Muḥammad al-Bāqir.
TABATABAI:17:40-55/r8.anchor: عن أبي حمزه قال كنا مع علي بن الحسين فمر بنا عصافير يصحن فقال أتدرون ما تقول هذه العصافير

TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet asked her to wash two garments; he explained that a garment praises God and ceases praising when soiled.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r1.anchor: أخرج الخطيب في تاريخه عن عائشة قالت دخل علي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال لي

TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r2.speaker: أنس
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r2.claim: Anas reports that animals and small creatures live for the duration of their praise, after which God takes their souls; the report says the Angel of Death has no part.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r2.anchor: أخرج العقيلي في الضعفاء وأبو الشيخ والديلمي عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r3.claim: The Angel of Death does not personally take these souls; other angels do so as intermediary causes.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r3.anchor: أنه لا يتصدى بنفسه قبض أرواحها وإنما يباشرها بعض الملائكة والأعوان

TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r4.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r4.claim: Muʿādh ibn Anas reports that the Prophet told riders to use mounts gently, not as seats for roadside conversation, since a mount may remember God more than its rider.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r4.anchor: عن معاذ بن أنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه مر على قوم وهم وقوف على دواب لهم

TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r5.speaker: السكوني
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r5.claim: Al-Sakūnī reports six rights of a mount from Abū ʿAbd Allāh: do not overburden or sit chatting on it, feed it first, do not brand or strike its face, and offer it water.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r5.anchor: قال للدابة على صاحبها ستة حقوق لا يحملها فوق طاقتها، ولا يتخذ ظهرها مجلسا

TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r6.speaker: علقمة وابن مسعود
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r6.claim: ʿAlqama and Ibn Masʿūd report hearing food praise while the Prophet ate; related reports say pebbles praised in his hand and testified to his prophethood before visitors from Ḥaḍramawt.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r6.anchor: علقمة وابن مسعود كنا نجلس مع النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ونسمع الطعام يسبح

TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة وجابر الأنصاري وابن عباس وأبي بن كعب وزين العابدين
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r7.claim: These authorities report that a tree trunk groaned when the Prophet moved to a pulpit, then quieted when he embraced it.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r7.anchor: أبو هريرة وجابر الأنصاري وابن عباس وأبي بن كعب وزين العابدين أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يخطب

TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the claim that universal praise consists of human-like audible languages with conventional words hidden from human senses.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#2/r8.anchor: فزعم أن هذا التسبيح العام من قبيل الأصوات، وأن لعامة الأشياء لغة أو لغات

TABATABAI:17:40-55#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:40-55#3/r1.claim: Creation's praise is literal speech: beings express their Lord's transcendence by manifesting the deficiency of their essences, attributes, and acts while knowing it.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#3/r1.anchor: أن لها تسبيحا هو كلام بحقيقة معنى الكلام وهو إظهارها تنزه ربها بإظهارها نقص ذاتها

TABATABAI:17:40-55#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:40-55#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:40-55#3/r2.claim: Those who hear pebbles or mountains praise perceive the real meaning inwardly, which their senses render as suitable words, as abstract realities appear in familiar dream images.
TABATABAI:17:40-55#3/r2.anchor: انما كان بإدراكهم تسبيحها الواقعي بحقيقة معناه من طريق الباطن

TABRISI:17:44/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:44/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والباقون
TABRISI:17:44/r1.claim: They differ between a light and a geminated reading of li-yadhdhakkarū; Abu Ali says it means reflection, not recollection after forgetting.
TABRISI:17:44/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم ليذكروا ساكنة الذال خفيفة

TABRISI:17:44/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:44/r2.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام وأبو بكر
TABRISI:17:44/r2.claim: They read 'as they say' with third-person ya; Basrans use second-person ta in the first phrase, with other variant combinations reported.
TABRISI:17:44/r2.anchor: وقرأ كما يقولون بالياء يسبح له بالياء أهل المدينة والشام وأبو بكر

TABRISI:17:44/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:44/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:44/r3.claim: 'Above what they say' may be coordinated with the preceding phrase or may independently declare God's transcendence; either ya or ta is sound in 'the heavens glorify.'
TABRISI:17:44/r3.anchor: فأما من قرأ سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون فإنه يحتمل وجهين

TABRISI:17:44/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:44/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:44/r4.claim: The Qur'an repeats proofs and examples so people reflect and recognize truth, yet unbelievers grow more distant and flee.
TABRISI:17:44/r4.anchor: أي كررنا الدلائل وفصلنا المعاني والأمثال وغير ذلك مما يوجب الاعتبار

TABRISI:17:44#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:44#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:44#2/r1.claim: Revelation establishes proof, removes excuses, benefits those who respond, and prevents worse corruption among those who reject it; unbelievers regard signs as tricks because they do not reflect.
TABRISI:17:44#2/r1.anchor: قيل الحكمة فيه إلزام الحجة وقطع المعذرة في إظهار الدلائل

TABRISI:17:44#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:44#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:44#2/r5.claim: All creation glorifies God by indicating His unity and justice; created things point to the eternal, self-sufficient maker.
TABRISI:17:44#2/r5.anchor: معنى التسبيح ها هنا الدلالة على توحيد الله وعدله وأنه لا شريك له

TABRISI:17:44#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:44#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:17:44#2/r6.claim: He says only living things glorify; Ibrahim and others say even animals, birds, and inanimate things such as a creaking door and flowing water do.
TABRISI:17:44#2/r6.anchor: وقيل إن معناه وما من شيء من الأحياء إلا يسبح بحمده عن الحسن

TABRISI:17:44#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:44#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:44#2/r7.claim: People fail to understand creation's glorification because they do not contemplate its signs; God delays punishment and forgives those who repent.
TABRISI:17:44#2/r7.anchor: لا تعلمون تسبيح هذه الأشياء حيث لم تنظروا فيها فتعلموا كيف دلالتها

THALABI:v6p102/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102/r1.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وحمزة والكسائي وحفص
THALABI:v6p102/r1.claim: They read تسبح with feminine tāʾ; other readers use masculine yāʾ, which Abū ʿUbayd prefers as agreement with the feminine subject.
THALABI:v6p102/r1.anchor: قرأ الحسن: وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وحمزة والكسائي وحفص: بالتاء، غيرهم: يسبح بالياء

THALABI:v6p102/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p102/r2.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God transcendent, obeying Him, affirming His lordship, and demonstrating His existence and oneness.
THALABI:v6p102/r2.anchor: ومعنى التسبيح التنزيه والطاعة والالتزام بالربوبية

THALABI:v6p102/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p102/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وإن من شيء حي

THALABI:v6p102/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102/r4.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
THALABI:v6p102/r4.claim: They say every ensouled thing glorifies God.
THALABI:v6p102/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن والضحاك: يعني كل شيء فيه الروح

THALABI:v6p102/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p102/r5.claim: Qatāda identifies the glorifying things as animals and plants.

THALABI:v6p102/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102/r6.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v6p102/r6.claim: A tree glorifies God, whereas a column does not.
THALABI:v6p102/r6.anchor: قال عكرمة: الشجرة تسبح والأسطوانة لا تسبح

THALABI:v6p102/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102/r7.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p102/r7.claim: When asked whether a dining table glorifies God, Hasan said it once did.
THALABI:v6p102/r7.anchor: فقال يزيد الرقاشي يا أبا سعيد يسبح هذا الخوان؟ فقال كان يسبح مرة

THALABI:v6p102/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p102/r9.claim: A damaged Prophetic report says a staff ceased glorifying after it had glorified.
THALABI:v6p102/r9.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: « [ما سبحت عصا إلا ترك] التسبيح»

THALABI:v6p102#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102#2/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
THALABI:v6p102#2/r1.claim: The Prophet taught that Noah instructed his son to say Glory and praise be to God, creation’s prayer and glorification and a means of provision.
THALABI:v6p102#2/r1.anchor: يا بني آمرك أن تقول: سبحان الله وبحمده فإنها صلاة الخلق وتسبيحهم

THALABI:v6p102#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102#2/r2.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v6p102#2/r2.claim: A damaged report says that every unidentified thing had glorified God for three hundred years.
THALABI:v6p102#2/r2.anchor: إلا وقد كان يسبح لله ثلاثمائة سنة

THALABI:v6p102#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102#2/r3.speaker: المقداد بن معد يكرب
THALABI:v6p102#2/r3.claim: A report says soil glorifies before wetting, nuts before moving, leaves on trees, water while unchanged, clothes when new, and animals while vocalizing.
THALABI:v6p102#2/r3.anchor: عن المقداد بن معد يكرب قال: إن التراب يسبح ما لم يبتل

THALABI:v6p102#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102#2/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v6p102#2/r4.claim: Pebbles glorified in the Prophet’s hand and in Abū Bakr’s, ʿUmar’s, and ʿUthmān’s, but not in the Companions’ hands.
THALABI:v6p102#2/r4.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأخذ كفا من حصى

THALABI:v6p102#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102#2/r5.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
THALABI:v6p102#2/r5.claim: A report says grapes and pomegranates glorified when the Prophet, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and ʿAlī ate, but not when an ordinary Companion did.
THALABI:v6p102#2/r5.anchor: وعن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه قال: «مرض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأتاه جبرئيل

THALABI:v6p102#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p102#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p102#2/r6.claim: People do not understand other things’ glorification because it is not expressed in their own languages and tongues.
THALABI:v6p102#2/r6.anchor: يعني لا تعلمون تسبيح ما عدا من تسبيح بلغاتكم وألسنتكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r1.claim: One interpretation takes praise literally: the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants praise God; the specification excludes devils and idol worshippers who do not truly praise him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أن المراد بالتسبيح هاهنا حقيقة التسبيح، فعلى هذا السموات السبع والأرضون تسبح لله تسبيحا حقيقيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r2.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r2.claim: Ikrima restricts the things that praise God to living things.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالي: {وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده} قال عكرمة: كل شيء حي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r3.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r3.claim: Hasan and al-Dahhak say everything with a soul praises God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r3.anchor: ونحوه قال الحسن والضحاك: كل شيء فيه الروح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the praising creatures as animals and growing things.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r5.claim: Some generalize praise to all created things, even a creaking ceiling or door, with each thing’s praise beyond human comprehension.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذا عام في كل شيء، وكل ما خلق الله فهو يسبح بحمده، وأن صرير السقف وصرير الباب من التسبيح لله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r6.claim: A second view takes praise as evidence that all things were created by a wise God free of defects; they submit and humble themselves, while disbelievers fail to infer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p344/r6.anchor: المذهب الثاني: أن المراد بالتسبيح هاهنا: الدلالة على أن الله -عز وجل- # خالق حكيم مبرأ من الأسواء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:44-46/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:44-46/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:44-46/r1.claim: Creation's glorification means all creatures point to God as wise Creator, free of imperfections; unbelievers fail to infer or reflect on this.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:44-46/r1.anchor: المراد بالتسبيح في هذه الآية الدلالة على أن الله سبحانه خالق حكيم مبرأ من الأسواء، والمخلوقون والمخلوقات كلها تدل على هذا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r1.claim: The earth and its inhabitants include believers and every creature that glorifies God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r1.anchor: {والأرض ومن فيهن} [الإسراء: 44] من المؤمنين، ومن يسبح له من الخلق.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r2.claim: A mountain’s uncut remainder glorifies God, but a piece severed from it does not; likewise a tree glorifies Him while its cut portion does not.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r2.anchor: كان الحسن يقول: إن الجبل يسبح، فإذا قطع منه شيء لم يسبح المقطوع ويسبح الأصل، وكذلك الشجرة ما قطع منها لم يسبح وتسبح هي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r3.claim: He links the warning to 16:61: if God punished people for their wrongdoing, He would withhold rain and destroy them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r3.anchor: كقوله: {ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بظلمهم ما ترك عليها من دابة} [النحل: 61] إذا يحبس القطر عنهم فأهلكهم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r4.claim: God forgives them if they repent.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r5.claim: God is forbearing toward creation and does not hasten as people hasten against one another; He forgives those who repent and return to the truth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p138/r5.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: {حليما} [الإسراء: 44] عن خلقه، فلا يعجل كعجلة بعضهم على بعض، {غفورا} [الإسراء: 44] لهم إذا تابوا وراجعوا الحق.

ELMALILI:17:44-52/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r1.speaker: çokları
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r1.claim: Most commentators understand all things as praising God through the testimony of their state, or by a mode broader than state and speech.
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r1.anchor: çokları bu tesbihin lisân-ı hâl ile delâlet veya hâl ü kālden e‘am olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:17:44-52/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r2.speaker: bazı müfessirîn
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r2.claim: Some commentators insist that the verse means literal verbal glorification.
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r2.anchor: bazı müfessirîn ma‘nâ-yı hakīkīsi üzere kavlen tesbih demek olduğunda ısrar etmiştir

ELMALILI:17:44-52/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r3.claim: Reports of stones glorifying in the Prophet’s hand and other transmitted reports support the literal-verbal interpretation.
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r3.anchor: taşların tesbîhi duyulması gibi birçok ehâdîs ve âsâr-ı vâride

ELMALILI:17:44-52/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r4.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî ve sâir birçok sûfiyye
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r4.claim: Ibn Arabi and many Sufis also accept literal verbal glorification.
ELMALILI:17:44-52/r4.anchor: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî ve sâir birçok sûfiyye dahi buna kāildirler

SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r1.claim: Abu Amr, the two Hamza/Kisai readers, and Hafs read feminine تسبح; others read masculine يسبح. Both work because the feminine is non-real and separated from its verb.
SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو والأخوان وحفص بالتاء، والباقون بالياء من تحت، وهما واضحتان؛

SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says a rational plural pronoun returns to the heavens and earth because they perform the rational act of glorifying; the author rejects his assumption that هن is restricted to rational beings, recalling 17:36.
SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " ثم أعاد على السماوات والأرض ضمير من يعقل لما أسند إليها فعل العاقل

SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r3.speaker: عبد الله والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r3.claim: Abdullah and al-Amash read the verb as feminine past سبحت.
SAMIN-DURR:17:44/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله والأعمش " سبحت " ماضيا بتاء التأنيث.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r1.claim: The seven heavens and all their inhabitants praise and worship God through their state, though people cannot understand their praise; the commentary refers to 2:29 for the heavens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r1.anchor: “Yedi gök” ile onlarda bulunan varlıkların hepsi hal lisanıyla Allah’ı tesbih eder, O’na ibadet eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r2.claim: Human intentional glorification is verbal or enacted through faith, worship, morals, and conduct that testify to God's unity and perfection and obey His law.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r2.anchor: Dil ile tesbih, hal ile tesbih. Birincisi, kulun Allah’ı her türlü eksiklikten tenzih ederek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r3.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r3.claim: Raghib calls this conscious, voluntary glorification, which belongs to beings with awareness and will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r3.anchor: Râgıb el-İsfahânî’nin iradî dediği tesbih olup şuurlu ve iradeli varlıklara mahsustur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r4.claim: Exegetes describe universal glorification in two ways: all things verbally praise God in their own language, or the cosmos obeys divine laws through its existence and operation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r4.anchor: Müfessirlere göre bu da iki çeşittir: 1. Dil ile tesbih. Her şey kendi diliyle Hakk’ı tesbih eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r5.claim: Even believers and unbelievers witness God's existence through the ordered operation of creation, from particles to galaxies.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r5.anchor: müminiyle münkiriyle bütün insanlar da Allah’ı tesbih ederler, varlığına tanıklık ederler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r6.claim: The verse about cosmic order follows the rejection of polytheism in verse 42 meaningfully and with deep wisdom.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r6.anchor: Putperestlerin inancındaki saçmalığı dile getiren 42. âyetin ardından evrenin düzenine işaret eden âyetin gelmesi son derece anlamlıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r7.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r7.claim: Razi argues that every constituent of an apple has determinate traits that only a powerful, wise determiner could assign, making each a complete proof of God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r7.anchor: bu parçacıklardan her biri Allah Teâlâ’nın varlığına tam ve başlı başına bir delildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r8.claim: People cannot comprehend creation's own language or fully know the number, qualities, and nature of atoms; scientific discovery grows while the unknown remains vast, as genetic code illustrates.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r8.anchor: Eşyanın kendilerine mahsus dil ile yaptığı tesbihi insanlar anlayamazlar; öte yandan atomların sayılarını, niteliklerini, mahiyetlerini de bütünüyle bilmek mümkün değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r9.claim: For God, halim means patient and not hasty to punish servants for sin and rebellion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r9.anchor: Allah için kullanıldığında “kullarının günah ve isyanları karşısında sabırlı, onları cezalandırmakta acele etmeyen” anlamına gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r10.claim: Halim is semantically close to divine names for forgiveness, awareness, power, and patience, including Afuv, Gafur, Tawwab, Habir, Muhsi, Wasi, Qadir, Qawi, Matin, Muqtadir, and Sabur.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:44/r10.anchor: Allah’ın halîm ismiyle “günahları bağışlayan, tövbeleri kabul eden” anlamındaki afüv, gafûr, tevvâb

ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r1.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r1.claim: One view says every created thing glorifies God, even the creaking of a roof or door; on this reading the address about not understanding is directed only to polytheists.
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r1.anchor: قيل إن كل ما خلق الله يسبح بحمده وإن صرير السقف وصرير الباب من التسبيح

ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r2.claim: Another possibility is that the glorification of these things is knowledge God has taught, and people understand only what He teaches them.
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r2.anchor: وجائز أن يكون تسبيح هذه الأشياء مما علم الله به، لايفقه منه إلا ما علمنا

ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r3.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r3.claim: Some say every thing signifies that God created it and that its wise Creator is free of defects; disbelievers fail to grasp this evidence in creation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: (وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده) أي ما من شيء إلا وفيه دليل أن الله خالقه

ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r4.claim: The author rejects that explanation: the people addressed already acknowledged God as their Creator, so they could not be unaware of the act of creation itself.
ZAJJAJ:v3p242/r4.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء لأن الذين خوطبوا بهذا كانوا مقرين بأن الله خالقهم

ASAD-NOTES:17:43#n52/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:43#n52/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:43#n52/r1.claim: Asad refers readers to his note on 2:20 for 'the seven heavens.'
ASAD-NOTES:17:43#n52/r1.anchor: For an explanation of this expression, see surah 2, note 20

ASAD-NOTES:17:43#n53/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:43#n53/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:43#n53/r1.claim: Creation testifies to a conscious creative will, but people are often blind and deaf to the evidence of God's ever-present power.
ASAD-NOTES:17:43#n53/r1.anchor: everything in creation bears witness to the existence of a conscious Creative Will, man is only too often blind and deaf

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p218/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p218/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p218/r3.claim: The tāʾ reading of tusabbiḥu is supported by Ubayy’s past-tense sabbaḥat; the yāʾ reading treats the heavens as a small plural that Arabic may make masculine.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p218/r3.anchor: والحجة لمن قرأ تسبح بالتاء قراءة أبي سبحت له السموات والحجة لمن قرأه بالياء

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p218/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p218/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p218/r4.claim: The author says a small plural precedes a large one and masculine precedes feminine, so agreement can follow the earlier form; examples include al-ashhur and niswah.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p218/r4.anchor: والعلة في ذلك أن الجمع القليل قبل الكثير والتذكير قبل التأنيث

IBNMUJAHID:v1p379/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p379/r6.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p379/r6.claim: Readers vary between yāʾ and tāʾ in the three forms: Ibn Kathīr uses yāʾ throughout; Nāfiʿ, Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir use tāʾ only at 17:42; further groupings continue in the next segment.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p379/r6.anchor: 12 واختلفوا فى قوله ﴿ لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون إذا لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا ﴾ 42

IBNMUJAHID:v1p381/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p381/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p381/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses tāʾ, yāʾ, tāʾ across the three forms; Ḥafṣ uses yāʾ in the first two and tāʾ in the third; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use tāʾ throughout.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p381/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو / ءالهة كما تقولون / بالتاء و ﴿ عما يقولون ﴾ بالياء ﴿ تسبح له ﴾ بالتاء

QIRAAT-ER:17:44:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:44:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:44:1#1/r1.claim: The masculine singular verb shifts agreement away from the feminine heavens, possibly agreeing with sabʿ or using the masculine default.
QIRAAT-ER:17:44:1#1/r1.anchor: Masculine singular verb — changes agreement from feminine (agreeing with samāwāt) to masculine

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p379/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p379/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p379/r1.claim: Qatāda says everything with a spirit glorifies God, including trees and other things that possess spirit.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p379/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم ﴾ قال كل شيء فيه الروح يسبح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p42/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p42/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p42/r1.claim: The verbal noun subḥān gives glorification absolute scope, without a time or agent and even before worshippers were created; opening the sūra this way suits its recurring tasbīḥ theme.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p42/r1.anchor: المجيء بالمصدر يفيد الإطلاق بدون تقيّد بزمن أو بفعل أو بفاعل تسبيح مطلق قبل تسبيح أحد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p890/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p890/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p890/r1.claim: The verse uses min with who glorifies and mā in other formulations; mā gathers all things, which is the rhetorical point of its wording.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p890/r1.anchor: والحكمة البيانية من ذلك جمع كل شيء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r1.speaker: المقدم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r1.claim: The presenter says earlier Arabs spoke their language naturally, while modern readers learn it only marginally, helping explain why they do not understand the Quran as earlier people did.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r1.anchor: استطراد من المقدم: لماذا لا نفهم نحن القرآن الآن كما فهموه في السابق؟

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r2.speaker: المقدم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r2.claim: Interpreting the Quran requires deep command of language, grammar, morphology, and rhetoric; slight familiarity is insufficient because conjunctions and case endings carry meaning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r2.anchor: العلماء يضعون للذي يتكلم في القرآن ويفسره شروطاً أولها التبحر في علوم اللغة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r3.claim: Hearing birds, thunder, or frogs does not mean grasping what their praise says or intends; hearing foreign speech likewise differs from understanding it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p997/r3.anchor: نحن نسمع التسبيح لكن لا نفقهه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p339/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p339/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p339/r2.claim: Humans cannot understand created beings' language and gestures as they glorify and pray; the author also points to 17:44 on this.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p339/r2.anchor: Human beings not being fully aware of their language and gestures though are not able to understand their glorification and prayers.

BURHAN:v3p380/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p380/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p380/r3.claim: The verse uses understand rather than simply know because fiqh conveys an increment beyond bare knowledge.
BURHAN:v3p380/r3.anchor: ولم يقل لا تعلمون لما في الفقه من الزيادة على العلم

ITQAN:v3p276/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p276/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p276/r2.claim: Because created things praise God without disobedience while the human addressees disobey, the close invokes forbearance and forgiveness; the cited hadith says punishment is held back by grazing beasts, bowed elders, and nursing infants.
ITQAN:v3p276/r2.anchor: لما كانت الأشياء كلها تسبح ولا عصيان في حقها وأنتم تعصون ختم به مراعاة للمقدر في الآية

ITQAN:v3p276/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p276/r3.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v3p276/r3.claim: An alternative reads the close as God being forbearing toward shortcomings in the praise of those who glorify Him and forgiving their sins.
ITQAN:v3p276/r3.anchor: وقيل التقدير حليما عن تفريط المسبحين غفورا لذنوبهم

ITQAN:v3p276/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p276/r4.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v3p276/r4.claim: Another explanation makes God forbearing toward the addressees who fail to understand the creatures' praise by neglecting reflection on His signs and creation.
ITQAN:v3p276/r4.anchor: وقيل حليما عن المخاطبين الذين لا يفقهون التسبيح بأهمالهم النظر في الآيات والعبر ليعرفوا حقه بالتأمل

BURHAN:v2p144/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p144/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p144/r7.claim: The author links the verses about creatures' glorification and human failure to comprehend it with God's wide forgiveness for those on earth who do not glorify or understand that praise.
BURHAN:v2p144/r7.anchor: ثم أعلم سبحانه سعة مغفرته لمن فى الأرض الذين لا يسبحونه ولا يفقهون تسبيح المسبحين

BURHAN:v4p7/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p7/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p7/r6.claim: The seven heavens are explicitly numbered in تسبيح له السماوات السبع because the heavens themselves glorify with their own beings.
BURHAN:v4p7/r6.anchor: أي تسبح بذواتها وأنفسها على اختلاف عددها ولهذا صرح بالعدد بقوله ﴿ السبع ﴾
